bugs.Bug: A vendor that was never invited can still put a bid into an event
bugs.What goes wrong: Procol is meant to let only the vendors a buyer invited take part in an event. A vendor company that was not invited was able to place a bid into a live event by using the 'bid on behalf of a vendor' route for its own company. Nothing checked that the vendor was in the event's invite list.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Publish an event and invite only Vendor A.
2. Sign in as Vendor B (not invited).
3. Place a bid on the event for Vendor B's own company through the on-behalf bid route.
bugs.What should happen: The bid is refused because Vendor B is not invited to the event.
bugs.What actually happens: The bid is accepted and saved on the event.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced with Procol's own test vendors on a test event; the app answered 'accepted' (HTTP 200).

bugs.Bug: A buyer can place a bid on behalf of a vendor who is not invited to the event
bugs.What goes wrong: When a buyer enters a bid on a vendor's behalf (a surrogate bid), Procol only checks that the buyer deals with that vendor in general. It does not check that the vendor is part of this event, so the buyer can add bids from vendors who were never invited.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Publish an event inviting Vendor A only.
2. As the buyer, place a surrogate bid for Vendor C, a vendor the company works with but did not invite to this event.
bugs.What should happen: The bid is refused because Vendor C is not invited to this event.
bugs.What actually happens: The bid is accepted and Vendor C now appears to have bid.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on both clients with test vendors; the app answered 'accepted' (HTTP 200).

bugs.Bug: A surrogate price is accepted for a vendor who never sent the required technical response
bugs.What goes wrong: In a two-round event (technical round, then price round) a vendor must answer the technical round before quoting a price. When the vendor tries this themselves Procol correctly refuses. When the buyer enters the price on the vendor's behalf, the same rule is skipped and the price is accepted.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Create an event with a technical round followed by a price round; invite two vendors.
2. Let neither vendor answer the technical round.
3. As the buyer, enter a price on behalf of one vendor.
bugs.What should happen: The price is refused until that vendor's technical response exists, the same as when the vendor tries it.
bugs.What actually happens: The price is accepted for a vendor who never qualified technically.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on both clients; the vendor's own attempt is refused, the on-behalf attempt is accepted (HTTP 200).

bugs.Bug: A vendor who declined the invitation can still bid
bugs.What goes wrong: When a vendor declines to participate (with a reason), Procol records the decision but never uses it. The same vendor can still open, price and submit a bid afterwards, so a 'declined' vendor can end up with the best price.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Invite a vendor to a live event.
2. As the vendor, decline participation with a reason.
3. As the same vendor, place and submit a bid.
bugs.What should happen: After declining, the vendor cannot bid (or must first change the decision back to 'participate').
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced with a test vendor; the decline was recorded and the later bid was accepted (HTTP 200).

bugs.Bug: Best-price and cost-breakdown requests are limited to the chosen vendors only on screen
bugs.What goes wrong: After bidding closes, a buyer can ask selected vendors for a best price or a cost breakdown. The limit to 'only these vendors' exists only in the screen. A vendor who was not asked can still revise and submit during that window, and the revision is accepted.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Close bidding on an event with two vendors.
2. Ask only Vendor 1 for a best price (or a cost breakdown).
3. As Vendor 2, who was not asked, revise and submit the bid during that window.
bugs.What should happen: Vendor 2's revision is refused because only Vendor 1 was asked.
bugs.What actually happens: Vendor 2's revision is accepted, for both the best-price and the cost-breakdown request.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced for both request types with test vendors; each revision was accepted (HTTP 200).

bugs.Bug: More than the requested quantity can be awarded when partial awarding is switched off
bugs.What goes wrong: With partial awarding switched off, a line's full quantity should go to one place and the total awarded can never exceed what was requested. Procol accepted an award giving the full quantity to two vendors at once, i.e. twice the requested quantity.
bugs.How to see it:
1. On a client with partial awarding off, run an event with two vendors bidding on one line item.
2. Create an award proposal that gives the full quantity to vendor 1 AND the full quantity to vendor 2.
bugs.What should happen: The proposal is refused because the awarded total is more than the requested quantity.
bugs.What actually happens: The proposal is accepted with double the quantity awarded.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on Demo Account 2 with test vendors; the app accepted the over-award (HTTP 200). The proposal was left unsubmitted.

bugs.Bug: One wrongly-typed field crashes an event update and then locks the event for every later update
bugs.What goes wrong: If an update to a live event sends a field in the wrong form — the title as a number, the attachments as plain text instead of a list, or 'show under open events' as the word 'yes' instead of yes/no — the server crashes. Worse, after that crash every later update to the same event also crashes, even a completely correct one, so the event can no longer be edited.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Publish a test event.
2. Update it with the title set to a number (e.g. 12345).
3. Now send a normal, correct update to the same event.
bugs.What should happen: Step 2 is refused with a clear message (e.g. 'title must be text') and the event keeps working normally.
bugs.What actually happens: Step 2 crashes the server, and step 3 (a correct update) crashes too.
bugs.How it was verified: Re-checked today on fresh test events, one per field, on PROCOL DEMO: each wrong field crashed and the following correct update crashed. The number-as-title crash was also recorded on Demo Account 2.

bugs.Bug: Sending an empty value instead of the vendor list or the round list crashes the update
bugs.What goes wrong: When an update to an event sends 'nothing' (an empty value) where the list of invited vendors or the list of rounds to publish should be, the server crashes instead of treating it as an empty list or asking for one.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Publish a test event.
2. Update it with the invited-vendor list (or the rounds list) sent as an empty value instead of a list.
bugs.What should happen: The update is refused with a clear message, or treated as an empty list.
bugs.How it was verified: Re-checked today, each on its own fresh test event; both crashed (the event kept working afterwards).

bugs.Bug: Withdrawing a live event without a proper remark crashes instead of asking for the remark
bugs.What goes wrong: A withdrawal is supposed to carry a remark explaining why. If the remark is missing — or is sent as a plain sentence instead of the remark details the product expects — the server crashes rather than telling the buyer what is needed. The event stays live.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Publish a test event.
2. Withdraw it without giving a withdrawal remark.
bugs.What should happen: The withdrawal is refused with a message like 'Please add a remark'.
bugs.What actually happens: The server crashes; the event is still live.
bugs.How it was verified: Re-checked today on clean test events on PROCOL DEMO (missing remark, and remark sent as plain text); the missing-remark crash was also recorded on Demo Account 2.

bugs.Bug: After a failed withdrawal, a correct withdrawal works but tells the buyer it failed
bugs.What goes wrong: Following the crash above, if the buyer tries again correctly (with a remark), the event IS withdrawn, but the server still answers with a crash. The buyer is told the withdrawal failed when it actually happened, which invites repeated attempts and confusion.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Publish a test event.
2. Withdraw it without a remark (crashes).
3. Withdraw it again, this time with a remark.
4. Open the event.
bugs.What should happen: Step 3 succeeds and says so.
bugs.What actually happens: Step 3 answers with a server error, yet the event shows as withdrawn in step 4.
bugs.How it was verified: Re-checked today on a clean test event: status before 'active', after the 'failed' call 'withdrawn'.

bugs.Bug: Reading an event's vendor list with a broken filter crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: The vendor (audience) list of an event accepts filters. If the filter text is malformed, the server crashes instead of ignoring it or saying the filter is invalid.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Publish a test event.
2. Open its vendor list with a malformed filter value.
bugs.What should happen: The filter is rejected with a clear message, or ignored.
bugs.How it was verified: Re-checked today on a fresh test event.

bugs.Bug: Many event screens crash on an id that does not exist instead of saying 'not found'
bugs.What goes wrong: Asking for something by an id that does not exist makes the server crash instead of answering 'not found'. Seen on: event details, the lots of an event (read, save draft, reset to smart lots), the auction leader board, the auction report, the counter-offer history, closing a bid and its approval flows, the surrogate-bid approval flows, quote-detail pages, the Master QCS for a proposal from another event, and a vendor opening a round that does not exist. Another screen of the same product answers 'not found' correctly for the same kind of request.
bugs.How to see it: Open any of the screens named above using an id that does not exist (for example an event or round that was never created).
bugs.What should happen: A clear 'not found' message.
bugs.How it was verified: Each re-checked on PROCOL DEMO; every crash reproduced on a second fresh event.

bugs.Bug: Creating or updating an event with an invalid status crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: When a new event is created with a status that is not allowed — an unknown word, the status 'withdrawn' (which is valid for an event but not for its line items), or a number — the server crashes instead of refusing the status. Updating a live event with an unknown status together with a settings change crashes the same way.
bugs.How to see it: Create a draft event with the status set to an unknown word (or 'withdrawn', or the number 1).
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a message such as 'invalid status'. Nothing is created.
bugs.How it was verified: Each variant replayed today on PROCOL DEMO and still crashes; the update variant re-checked on a clean test event.

bugs.Bug: Creating an event with a malformed line item crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: When creating an event, a line item that is not in the expected shape crashes the server: the line items sent as text instead of a list, a line item that is plain text, a line item with no product, or a line item whose product does not exist.
bugs.How to see it: Create a draft event where the line item has no product (or the product does not exist, or the line items are sent as text).
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a clear message such as 'product is required' or 'product not found'. Nothing is created.
bugs.How it was verified: All four variants replayed today on PROCOL DEMO and still crash; the non-existent-product and malformed-list variants were also recorded on Demo Account 2.

bugs.Bug: Creating an event with the settings, description or attachments in the wrong form crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: When creating an event, sending the event settings as a list or as text (instead of a set of options), the description as a number, or the attachments as plain text items crashes the server.
bugs.How to see it: Create a draft event with the description set to a number (or the settings sent as text, or attachments as plain text).
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a clear message, or the value stored as text. Nothing broken is created.
bugs.How it was verified: All variants replayed today on PROCOL DEMO and still crash.

bugs.Bug: Four templates offered in the template chooser crash when opened
bugs.What goes wrong: Some templates that Procol lists as available to choose for a round fail with a server crash as soon as they are opened, so they can never be used. On PROCOL DEMO: 'test template for event detailed', 'test_rfi_template' and 'test_rfi_template_v2'. On Demo Account 2: '123'.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Open the list of templates for a new round.
2. Open one of the templates named in this row.
bugs.What should happen: The template opens, or a broken template is not offered at all.
bugs.How it was verified: Each template opened on 1 Oct 2026 by the template check; every open crashed.

bugs.Bug: Adding a price round whose line item has no product crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: When a price (RFQ) round is added to an event and its line item carries no product, the server crashes instead of saying the product is missing.
bugs.How to see it: Add a price round to a draft event where the line item has no product.
bugs.What should happen: Refused with 'product is required'.
bugs.How it was verified: Recorded 7 times on 1 Oct 2026 across both clients.

bugs.Bug: Adding a technical round with a form page that has no name crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: When a technical (RFP) round is added and one page of its questionnaire has no name, the server crashes instead of asking for a page name.
bugs.How to see it: Add a technical round to a draft event with a questionnaire page left without a name.
bugs.What should happen: Refused with 'page name is required'.
bugs.How it was verified: Recorded 5 times on 1 Oct 2026 across both clients.

bugs.Bug: A round can be created with a template that does not exist
bugs.What goes wrong: A price round was saved even though it named a template that does not exist. The event then carries a round with no real template behind it, which breaks later steps (for example awarding failed afterwards with 'bid not present on this line item').
bugs.How to see it: Add a price round to a draft event, naming a template that does not exist.
bugs.What should happen: Refused with 'template not found'.
bugs.What actually happens: The round is accepted and saved.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on two templates per client on 1 Oct 2026 (accepted, HTTP 200).

bugs.Bug: Creating a product category with an invalid level crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: A product category must be created at a known level (category / sub-category, etc.). Sending an unknown level such as 'supercategory', or the right word in capitals ('CATEGORY'), crashes the server instead of refusing it.
bugs.How to see it: Create a product category with the level set to 'supercategory' (or 'CATEGORY').
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a message listing the allowed levels.
bugs.How it was verified: Replayed today on PROCOL DEMO and still crashes; also recorded on Procol Sandbox Demo (PO).

bugs.Bug: Creating a delivery location without a city, or with an unknown location type, crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: A delivery location needs a city and a known location type. Leaving out the city, or using a type the system does not have (e.g. 'warehouse_center'), crashes the server instead of asking for the missing or correct value.
bugs.How to see it: Create a delivery location without choosing a city (or with an unknown location type).
bugs.What should happen: Refused with 'city is required' / 'invalid location type'.
bugs.How it was verified: Both variants replayed today on PROCOL DEMO and still crash.

bugs.Bug: Creating a team with an unknown team type crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: Creating a team with a team type the system does not know (e.g. 'procurement') crashes the server instead of refusing it.
bugs.How to see it: Create a team with the team type set to 'procurement'.
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a message listing the allowed team types.
bugs.How it was verified: Replayed today on PROCOL DEMO and still crashes.

bugs.Bug: Creating a user with an unknown or wrongly-capitalised role crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: Adding a user with a role that does not exist (e.g. 'owner') or the right role in capitals (e.g. 'SUPER_ADMIN') crashes the server instead of refusing the role.
bugs.How to see it: Add a new user with the role 'owner' (or 'SUPER_ADMIN').
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a message listing the allowed roles. No user is created.
bugs.How it was verified: Both variants replayed today on PROCOL DEMO and still crash; also recorded on Procol Sandbox Demo (PO).

bugs.Bug: The purchase-request list crashes when its filter is malformed
bugs.What goes wrong: The purchase-request list accepts filters. A malformed filter crashes the server instead of being rejected or ignored.
bugs.How to see it: Open the purchase-request list with a malformed filter value.
bugs.What should happen: The filter is rejected with a clear message, or ignored.
bugs.How it was verified: Replayed today on PROCOL DEMO and still crashes; also recorded on Procol Sandbox Demo (PO).

bugs.Bug: Searching the events list sometimes shows the wrong, unfiltered results
bugs.What goes wrong: When a buyer types an event title into the events-list search quickly, the screen sometimes shows the ten most recent events instead of the one that matches, while the search box still shows the title. The server sends the right single result, but an older, slower 'all events' answer arrives later and overwrites it on screen.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Open Events.
2. As soon as the search box appears, type the exact title of one event.
3. Look at the list.
bugs.What should happen: Only the matching event is listed.
bugs.What actually happens: In about 5 of 9 tries, ten unrelated recent events are listed instead.
bugs.How it was verified: Seen in 5 of 9 fast searches with network evidence (the late unfiltered answer arrives after the search answer); 0 of 9 when the list was allowed to load first.

bugs.Bug: Durations with seconds are shown wrongly (e.g. '0 second' for a 45-second window)
bugs.What goes wrong: The event overview shows Order Duration and Evaluation Time. Whenever a duration has leftover seconds, the seconds part is calculated from the minutes instead, so a 45-second window shows '0 second' and 30 minutes 15 seconds would show '30 mins 30 seconds'.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Open the overview of an event whose bidding window or evaluation time includes seconds.
2. Read Order Duration / Evaluation Time.
bugs.What should happen: The real duration (e.g. '45 seconds').
bugs.How it was verified: Seen on a test event and confirmed in the app's code: the seconds part counts minutes.

bugs.Bug: Invited vendors are labelled 'Not Participated' while bidding is still open
bugs.What goes wrong: In the participants table, a vendor who has been invited but has not bid yet is always shown as 'Not Participated', even while bidding is still open. Elsewhere the product calls this state 'Pending', so the buyer is told the vendor has dropped out when they may still bid.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Publish an event and invite a vendor.
2. Before the vendor bids, open the event's participants table.
bugs.What should happen: The vendor shows as 'Pending' (invited, not yet responded).
bugs.How it was verified: Seen on a test event and confirmed in the app's code (the text is fixed for every invited vendor).

bugs.Bug: A GST of 0% is shown as a dash, as if nothing was entered
bugs.What goes wrong: In the responses grid, a vendor's GST of 0 is displayed as '–', which looks like the vendor left it empty.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Have a vendor bid with GST 0.
2. Open the event's responses grid.
bugs.What should happen: '0%' is shown.
bugs.How it was verified: Seen on a test event; the server sent 0 for GST.

bugs.Bug: Extending the bidding time after an award proposal shows a misleading message about auctions
bugs.What goes wrong: Once an award proposal has been submitted, extending the bidding time is correctly blocked, but the message says 'You cannot edit rfq once the auction is created' even on events that have no auction, so the buyer does not learn the real reason.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Run an event to the award stage and submit a proposal.
2. Try to extend the bidding time.
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a message saying time cannot be extended after an award proposal.
bugs.What actually happens: Refused with 'You cannot edit rfq once the auction is created'.
bugs.How it was verified: Seen on both clients during the bidding scenarios.

bugs.Bug: Scoring before the technical round has closed says 'Order not active'
bugs.What goes wrong: An evaluator who tries to score a technical response while the technical round is still open is correctly stopped, but the message 'Order not active' does not explain that scoring opens only after the round closes.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Open a technical round to vendors.
2. Before it closes, try to score a vendor's response as the evaluator.
bugs.What should happen: A message such as 'Scoring opens when the technical round closes'.
bugs.How it was verified: Seen on both clients during the evaluation scenario.

bugs.Bug: Filtering the purchase-request list by two statuses at once crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: Filtering purchase requests by 'open' and 'in progress' together — an ordinary filter a buyer uses — crashes the server. Unknown status values, a status sent as plain text and an unknown closure type crash the same way instead of being refused.
bugs.How to see it: Open the purchase-request list and filter by the statuses 'open' and 'in progress' together.
bugs.What should happen: Purchase requests in either status are listed.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on two separate runs.

bugs.Bug: A round's approval timeline crashes when filtered by two approval types
bugs.What goes wrong: Reading the approval timeline of a round filtered by two approval types — a normal filter — crashes the server. A malformed filter or the approval type sent as plain text crashes it too.
bugs.How to see it: Open a round's approvals and filter by two approval types at once.
bugs.What should happen: The approvals of both types are listed.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on two separate runs.

bugs.Bug: The change history of a round crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: Opening the change history (all versions) of an ordinary round crashes the server. Asking for a negative page or an unbounded number of rows crashes it as well.
bugs.How to see it: Open the change history of a published round.
bugs.What should happen: The round's versions are listed.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on two separate runs.

bugs.Bug: Downloading the event details of a closed price round crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: The 'download event details' action on a price round that has closed crashes the server, so the buyer cannot download them. Asking for the same download for a vendor company that is not in the event crashes too.
bugs.How to see it: Open a closed price round and download its event details.
bugs.What should happen: The file downloads.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on two separate runs.

bugs.Bug: Reading a round together with a bid's history crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: Reading a price round while asking for the history of its own bid crashes the server. An unknown or non-numeric bid crashes the same way instead of being refused.
bugs.How to see it: Open a price round that has a bid, asking for that bid's history.
bugs.What should happen: The round and the bid's history are shown.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on two separate runs.

bugs.Bug: Editing a published event's title says it worked but does not change the title
bugs.What goes wrong: Changing the title of a published event answers 'success', but reading the event back — as the buyer or as an invited vendor — still shows the old title. The buyer is told the change was saved when it was not.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Publish an event.
2. Change its title.
3. Open the event again (as the buyer, then as the vendor).
bugs.What should happen: The new title is shown everywhere.
bugs.What actually happens: The old title is still shown, although the change was reported as successful.
bugs.How it was verified: Found by the API test compiler; reproduced on a second fresh event (read back as buyer and as vendor).

bugs.Bug: A draft with no rounds can be published
bugs.What goes wrong: Publishing an event that has no rounds attached is accepted, producing a live event in which vendors have nothing to respond to.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Create a draft event and add no rounds.
2. Publish it.
bugs.What should happen: Refused: an event needs at least one round to be published.
bugs.What actually happens: Accepted; the event goes live with no rounds.
bugs.How it was verified: Found by the API test compiler; reproduced on a second fresh event.

bugs.Bug: Editing a live event crashes on a malformed line item, terms or delivery schedule
bugs.What goes wrong: While editing a live event, line items sent as plain text, a line item with a product that does not exist, an empty line-item row, terms with an extra unknown field, or an unknown delivery schedule all crash the server instead of being refused.
bugs.How to see it: Edit a live event and send a line item whose product does not exist (or an empty row).
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a clear message; the event is unchanged.
bugs.How it was verified: Each reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on two separate runs.

bugs.Bug: Converting a price round to an auction crashes on incomplete or malformed details
bugs.What goes wrong: Converting an RFQ round into an auction crashes the server when the details are incomplete or in the wrong form: an unknown auction type, an empty or text item row, a row with no variant or quantity, no auction end time, settings sent as text, a trigger time as text, a serial row with no times, or a knockout round length as text.
bugs.How to see it: Convert a published price round to an auction without giving the auction's end time.
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a message naming what is missing or wrong.
bugs.How it was verified: 13 variants, each reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on two separate runs.

bugs.Bug: Counter offers crash on unexpected input instead of refusing it
bugs.What goes wrong: Raising, bulk-raising, resolving and revoking counter offers all crash the server when the request is not in the expected shape — for example a price sheet sent as an object, a row with no creator quantity, rows sent as plain text, or the request list sent as text or numbers. Reading the history of a counter offer that does not exist also crashes.
bugs.How to see it: Raise a counter offer on a vendor's bid where a price row has no creator quantity.
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a clear message.
bugs.How it was verified: 14 variants, each reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on two separate runs.

bugs.Bug: Event, history, draft, export and purchase-order lists crash on malformed filters
bugs.What goes wrong: The events list, events history, drafts list, bulk export, purchase-order list and an event's line-item search all crash the server when a filter is malformed or of the wrong type (for example statuses sent as text, a quantity sent as a list, product ids sent as text, an out-of-range start).
bugs.How to see it: Open the events history with the 'statuses' filter sent as plain text.
bugs.What should happen: The filter is refused with a clear message, or ignored.
bugs.How it was verified: 15 variants across six lists, each reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on two separate runs.

bugs.Bug: Saving a lot plan crashes on malformed input
bugs.What goes wrong: Saving a draft lot plan crashes the server when the lots are sent as a list instead of the expected form, as plain text, or with an empty item list.
bugs.How to see it: Save a draft lot plan with the lots sent as plain text.
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a clear message.
bugs.How it was verified: Each reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on two separate runs.

bugs.Bug: Lot plans accept another event's round and line items
bugs.What goes wrong: The lot plan of one event can be built from a different event's price round, and saved with line items that belong to another event. Both are accepted, so one event's lot plan ends up holding another event's data.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Have two test events.
2. Ask for the lots of event A using event B's price round (or save event A's lot plan with event B's line items).
bugs.What should happen: Refused: the round and line items must belong to this event.
bugs.What actually happens: Accepted, and the lots are built and saved across the two events.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on two separate runs (test events only).

bugs.Bug: Unsupported report and comparison views answer 'success' with nothing in them
bugs.What goes wrong: Asking for a report type that does not exist, or a Master QCS view type that does not exist, answers 'success' with an empty result instead of saying the request is not valid.
bugs.How to see it: Request a report with an unsupported type.
bugs.What should happen: Refused: the report type is not supported.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on two separate runs.

bugs.Bug: Entering a price on a vendor's behalf crashes when a price line has no creator quantity
bugs.What goes wrong: A surrogate bid (the buyer entering a vendor's price) crashes the server when a price line has no 'creator quantity', or when the vendor company is missing, instead of refusing the request.
bugs.How to see it: As the buyer, enter a price on an invited vendor's behalf with a price line that has no creator quantity.
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a clear message.
bugs.How it was verified: Pinned by sending the working request with one field changed at a time; reproduced three times on fresh events.

bugs.Bug: Adding a technical round without a questionnaire crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: A technical (RFP) round is the round where vendors answer a questionnaire. When such a round is added with no questionnaire at all, with an empty questionnaire list, or with a price sheet sent in place of the questionnaire, the server crashes instead of saying a questionnaire is required.
bugs.How to see it: Add a technical round to a draft event and leave out its questionnaire (or send an empty one).
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a clear message such as 'add at least one form to the technical round'. Nothing is saved.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3 Oct 2026: every variant listed failed the same way twice, each time on its own fresh test event.

bugs.Bug: Adding a technical round with an incomplete questionnaire crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: When the questionnaire of a technical round is incomplete, the server crashes instead of pointing at the missing part. Seen with: a vendor-assessment form that has no questions, a form whose pages have no headings, and a tab that has no sections.
bugs.How to see it: Add a technical round to a draft event whose vendor-assessment form has no questions (or whose pages have no headings, or a tab with no sections).
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a message naming what is missing.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3 Oct 2026: every variant listed failed the same way twice, each time on its own fresh test event.

bugs.Bug: Adding a price round with an incomplete price sheet crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: The price sheet of a price (RFQ) round lists the columns vendors fill in and the items they price. When it is incomplete, the server crashes instead of refusing it. Seen with: a sheet that has no columns, a drop-down column with no options to choose from, and an item row with no product variant.
bugs.How to see it: Add a price round to a draft event whose price sheet has a drop-down column with no options (or no columns at all, or an item with no variant).
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a message naming what is missing.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3 Oct 2026: every variant listed failed the same way twice, each time on its own fresh test event.

bugs.Bug: Adding an auction round with an invalid auction setting crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: When an auction round is added with an auction setting outside the allowed choices or in the wrong form, the server crashes instead of refusing the setting. Seen with: an auction strategy that does not exist, the knockout step written as text instead of a number, the time-extension trigger written as text or as a fraction (e.g. 2.5 minutes), the 'basket auction' switch written as the word "false" instead of off, and a basket auction whose items carry no per-item terms.
bugs.How to see it: Add an auction round to a draft event with the auction strategy set to a value that does not exist (or the extension trigger set to 2.5).
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a message such as 'invalid auction strategy' or 'extension trigger must be a whole number of minutes'.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3 Oct 2026: every variant listed failed the same way twice, each time on its own fresh test event.

bugs.Bug: Adding a round with its timings in the wrong form crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: When a round is added with a closing time that is not a real date-time, or as a staggered round (where each item closes at its own time) without the per-item times, the server crashes instead of asking for valid times.
bugs.How to see it: Add a staggered round to a draft event without giving each item its own closing time.
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a message asking for the missing or invalid times.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3 Oct 2026: every variant listed failed the same way twice, each time on its own fresh test event.

bugs.Bug: Adding a round with invalid currency settings crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: When a round's currency settings list no allowed currencies, or name a base currency that is not among the allowed ones, the server crashes. The second case should be a simple refusal: the base currency must be one the vendors are allowed to quote in.
bugs.How to see it: Add a round to a draft event whose base currency is not in its list of allowed currencies.
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a message such as 'base currency must be one of the allowed currencies'.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3 Oct 2026: every variant listed failed the same way twice, each time on its own fresh test event.

bugs.Bug: Adding a round with other settings in the wrong form crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: Several round settings crash the server when they arrive in the wrong form instead of being refused: an unknown round status, the evaluators written as plain text instead of a list of people, the savings options sent as a list, the auto-award settings sent as text, and the invited-vendor list sent as an empty value.
bugs.How to see it: Add a round to a draft event with the evaluators written as plain text (or any other variant listed).
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a clear message naming the setting.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3 Oct 2026: every variant listed failed the same way twice, each time on its own fresh test event.

bugs.Bug: Adding a technical or auction round with a template that does not exist crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: A price round that names a template that does not exist is wrongly accepted (see the row 'A round can be created with a template that does not exist'). A technical round or an auction round naming a template that does not exist goes further and crashes the server.
bugs.How to see it: Add a technical round (or an auction round) to a draft event, naming a template that does not exist.
bugs.What should happen: Refused with 'template not found'.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3 Oct 2026: every variant listed failed the same way twice, each time on its own fresh test event.

bugs.Bug: Changing a round's status to an unknown value crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: Updating a single round of an event with a status word that does not exist (for example 'banana') crashes the server instead of refusing the status. This is about a round; the open question about the same mistake on the whole event is on the 'To confirm' tab.
bugs.How to see it: Publish a test event, then update one of its rounds with the status set to a word that does not exist.
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a message such as 'invalid status'. The round is unchanged.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3 Oct 2026: every variant listed failed the same way twice, each time on its own fresh test event.

bugs.Bug: A vendor's answer to 'will you participate?' crashes on an unknown choice
bugs.What goes wrong: An invited vendor tells the buyer whether they will take part (participate or decline). When the answer sent is not one of those choices (for example 'maybe'), the server crashes instead of refusing it.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Invite a QA vendor to a live event.
2. As the vendor, answer the participation question with a choice that does not exist.
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a message such as 'choose participate or decline'.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3 Oct 2026: every variant listed failed the same way twice, each time on its own fresh test event.

bugs.Bug: A vendor reaching the buyer's 'bid on behalf of a vendor' route crashes it
bugs.What goes wrong: Entering a bid on a vendor's behalf is a buyer action. A vendor's own login can still reach that route, and with an ordinary request it crashes the server instead of being told it is not allowed. The row 'A vendor that was never invited can still put a bid into an event' shows the same route also lets vendors in.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Invite a QA vendor to a live event.
2. Signed in as that vendor, send a bid through the buyer's 'bid on behalf of a vendor' route.
bugs.What should happen: Refused with 'you are not allowed to perform this action'.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3 Oct 2026: every variant listed failed the same way twice, each time on its own fresh test event.

bugs.Bug: The Overview tab shows the wrong number of seconds for a stage's duration and evaluation time
bugs.What goes wrong: On a stage's Overview tab, Order Configurations shows how long bidding lasts and how long evaluation lasts. The seconds part is wrong: the screen prints the minutes figure in place of the seconds. A window of 2 minutes 50 seconds reads '2 mins 2 seconds', and a 10-second evaluation time reads '0 second'. The backend sends the right times; only the screen's wording is wrong.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Open a published event and click one of its stages.
2. Open the Overview tab and read Order Duration and Evaluation Time.
3. Compare them with the stage's start, end and extra closing time.
bugs.What should happen: The durations read correctly, e.g. '2 mins 50 seconds' and '10 seconds'.
bugs.What actually happens: The seconds are wrong: '2 mins 2 seconds' and '0 second'.
bugs.How it was verified: Seen on 8 fresh test events (4 per client), comparing what the backend sent with what the screen shows. The console's duration formatter prints the minutes value as the seconds (utils/index.js:567-568).

bugs.Bug: On the award proposal page, the Participants list is numbered 'NaN' instead of 1, 2, 3
bugs.What goes wrong: The award proposal page has a Participants panel listing the invited vendors. Its 'S No.' column shows 'NaN' (not a number) on every row instead of 1, 2, 3, because the page uses the participants table without telling it which page of the list it is on.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Open an event that has an award proposal.
2. Open Master QCS and click 'Bid Selection Proposal'.
3. Open the Participants panel and read the S No. column.
bugs.What should happen: The rows are numbered 1, 2, 3 …
bugs.How it was verified: Seen on 7 fresh test events (4 on Demo Account 2, 3 on PROCOL DEMO). Cause in the console code: projectProposal.jsx:1175 renders the table without a page number, which participantsTable.jsx:153-155 needs for the numbering.

bugs.Bug: The Price Trends tab fails with a server crash on Demo Account 2
bugs.What goes wrong: A pricing or auction stage has a Price Trends tab that shows past deals for the same products. On Demo Account 2 the request behind this tab crashes on the server for every stage, so no past prices can ever be shown there. The same tab works on PROCOL DEMO.
bugs.How to see it:
1. On Demo Account 2, open any pricing or auction stage.
2. Click the Price Trends tab.
bugs.What should happen: Past deals for the stage's products are listed (or 'no past deals').
bugs.What actually happens: The server crashes and no price history is shown.
bugs.How it was verified: The price-trends request answered with a server error on 4 of 4 fresh test events on Demo Account 2; PROCOL DEMO answered normally for the same kind of stage.

bugs.Bug: Every vendor can read every competitor's prices on a sealed RFQ
bugs.What goes wrong: In a sealed RFQ a vendor must never see what other vendors quoted. Procol stores each vendor's unit price for every line in a shared record, labelled with that vendor's company id, and sends this record to every vendor when they open the event. The screen does not show it, but it is in the data the app sends to each vendor's browser, so any vendor can read all its competitors' prices line by line — including prices the buyer entered on a vendor's behalf. The same prices are also in the round's page data, reach vendors that never bid, stay visible after the award, and defeat a rank-only auction (where vendors should see only their rank).
bugs.How to see it:
1. Create an RFQ with two or more line items and invite three or more vendors.
2. Let the vendors bid (or enter a bid on one vendor's behalf as the buyer).
3. Sign in as any one vendor and open the RFQ.
4. Look at the data the app sent for each line item.
bugs.What should happen: Each vendor receives only its own prices — nothing about other vendors' prices, totals or company ids.
bugs.What actually happens: Each vendor receives every other vendor's unit price for every line, labelled by the competitor's company id.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on 12 fresh test events (RFQs and rank auctions) on both clients, and re-checked independently by signing in as two different QA vendors: each saw the prices of the 3 other vendors. Cause: bid_trade_product.rb:121-131 writes every vendor's price into the line item's shared record, which is sent to every caller.

bugs.Bug: A vendor can give a discount above 100%, which makes its bid total negative and the best bid
bugs.What goes wrong: On a bid sheet where the vendor enters a discount %, Procol accepts any number — 150% included. The bid total then becomes negative (here −₹6,503), and that negative total is shown to the buyer as the event's best bid. A discount must be between 0 and 100%; that check exists only on Procol's older bid screens, not on the bid sheet.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Create an RFQ whose bid sheet has a vendor-entered 'Discount %' field.
2. Invite several vendors; let some bid normally.
3. As one vendor, quote normal prices with a discount of 150%.
4. Open the comparison as the buyer.
bugs.What should happen: A discount above 100% is refused, so no bid total can be negative or rank first.
bugs.What actually happens: The 150% discount is accepted, the bid total is −₹6,503.28, and it is shown as the event's best bid.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on 4 fresh test events across both clients; the negative total matches an independent recalculation exactly. The 0–100% check runs only on the older bid paths (bids_controller.rb:555-560). Entered through the vendor's API; whether the vendor screen also blocks it was not checked.

bugs.Bug: Asking for a report with an unknown report type crashes the server
bugs.What goes wrong: When the comparison report is requested with a report type that does not exist (for example 'excel_report'), the server crashes instead of refusing the request. The same request without the report type returns the report normally.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Open an RFQ that has bids.
2. Request its comparison report with the report type set to a value that does not exist.
bugs.What should happen: Refused with a clear message, or the report is returned.
bugs.How it was verified: Seen on 2 fresh test events on PROCOL DEMO (3 requests). Likely cause: an unknown value for the report type (report.rb:24) — read from the code, not traced in the server logs.

bugs.Bug: Every invited vendor can see who else bid, their bid status and who won
bugs.What goes wrong: In a sealed event a vendor must not learn who its competitors are. The data Procol sends each invited vendor for a round lists every bidder: the competitor's company name, its company id, its bid id, its bid status (for example 'selected' — i.e. who won) and how many times it revised its bid. Even a vendor that never bid receives it, and it stays visible after the award. Together with the price leak (the row 'Every vendor can read every competitor's prices on a sealed RFQ') a vendor can put a name to every competitor's price.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Publish an RFQ or auction and invite several vendors; let some of them bid.
2. Sign in as any invited vendor (even one that has not bid) and open the round.
3. Look at the data the app sent for the round's page.
bugs.What should happen: A vendor receives only its own bid's details; competitors are never named or described.
bugs.What actually happens: Every other bidder is listed by company name with its bid id, bid status (including who was selected) and revision count.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on 10 fresh test events on both clients (RFQs and auctions), and re-checked independently by signing in as a QA vendor who never bid: it saw the three other vendors by name, with bid ids and 'selected' status. Served by api/v1/trade_controller.rb:371 via trade_template_helper.rb:5856-5900.

bugs.Bug: Splitting a line's award between vendors creates purchase orders for each vendor's full quantity
bugs.What goes wrong: When a 30 KG line is awarded across three vendors (15, 10 and 5 KG), Procol creates three purchase orders of 30 KG each — 90 KG ordered for a 30 KG need. The prices on the orders are right; the quantities are each vendor's whole quote instead of the part awarded to it. This happens when the comparison template does not mark the awarded quantity as a field the buyer edits, although the company has partial awarding switched on.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Create an RFQ for one line of 30 KG and invite three vendors; let each quote for 30 KG.
2. Award the line split 15 / 10 / 5 KG across the three vendors and get it approved.
3. Create the purchase orders from the award and read their quantities.
bugs.What should happen: The orders carry 15, 10 and 5 KG — 30 KG in total, as awarded.
bugs.What actually happens: Each order carries 30 KG — 90 KG in total.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on 4 fresh test events on PROCOL DEMO. The order quantity comes from the vendor's quoted quantity when awarded quantity is not a buyer-editable field (proposal_helper.rb:1177-1190, bid_concern.rb:7-9, order.rb:300-306).

bugs.Bug: Taking a vendor off a split award subtracts its whole quote, so the award total is wrong
bugs.What goes wrong: When a buyer removes one vendor from a line that is split between several vendors (the way the award screen does it), Procol subtracts that vendor's whole quote from the award total instead of only the part awarded to it. In the test the total went to −₹1,550, and to ₹22,705 after the vendor was added back, instead of ₹1,43,980. The award was then approved with that wrong total — and the total decides which approval flow applies.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Award one line split across three vendors.
2. Remove one of the vendors from the award, then add it back.
3. Read the award total.
bugs.What should happen: The total changes by the removed vendor's awarded amount only, and returns to ₹1,43,980 when it is added back.
bugs.What actually happens: The total becomes −₹1,550, then ₹22,705, and the award can be approved with it.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on 2 fresh test events on PROCOL DEMO. The award value removed is the vendor's whole bid total (proposal_helper.rb, get_po_value_to_be_added falls back to the bid's gross total).

bugs.Bug: Vendors tied at the lowest price are counted as 'not L1' in the award
bugs.What goes wrong: When two vendors quote the same lowest price, the award summary counts neither of them as L1: the L1 value shows ₹0 and the tied vendors' amounts are counted under 'non-L1'.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Create an RFQ and let two vendors quote the same lowest price.
2. Award the line to one of them and read the award's L1 / non-L1 values.
bugs.What should happen: The tied vendors are L1, so the L1 value is the awarded amount.
bugs.What actually happens: L1 shows ₹0 and the award is counted as non-L1.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on 6 fresh test events across both clients (proposal_helper.rb:994-1001, bid_rank_helper.rb:215-218).

bugs.Bug: A vendor's awarded quantity cannot be lowered once a line is fully awarded
bugs.What goes wrong: When a line is fully awarded across vendors and the buyer lowers one vendor's quantity, Procol refuses with 'You cannot select bid with more than requested quantity', because it counts that vendor's current award as well as the new, lower quantity. The only way round it is to remove the vendor and add it again, which triggers the wrong-total problem in the row above.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Award a 30 KG line as 15 / 10 / 5 KG.
2. Change the 5 KG vendor's quantity to 3 KG.
bugs.What should happen: The change is accepted (3 KG is within the requested 30 KG).
bugs.What actually happens: Refused: 'You cannot select bid with more than requested quantity'.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on 4 fresh test events on PROCOL DEMO (proposal_helper.rb:1295-1305).

bugs.Bug: After an auction's automatic extension, existing bids still show the old end time
bugs.What goes wrong: When a late bid makes an auction extend automatically, the auction's end time moves, but the bids already placed keep the old end time as their 'valid till' time.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Run an auction with automatic extension and several vendors bidding.
2. Place a winning bid in the last minutes so the auction extends.
3. Read the earlier bids' end ('valid till') time.
bugs.What should happen: Every bid shows the auction's new end time.
bugs.What actually happens: The earlier bids keep the old end time.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on 4 fresh test events across both clients (bid.rb:2264-2286 keeps the cached schedule).

bugs.Bug: A vendor can read the weight the buyer gave a competing vendor
bugs.What goes wrong: In weighted bidding the buyer gives each vendor a weight that changes how its price is ranked. These weights are the buyer's private assessment. When a vendor opens the round, the data Procol sends it includes the weight the buyer set for every other vendor, not just its own.
bugs.How to see it:
1. On a live RFQ with weighted bidding, give QA vendor 1 a weight of 100 and QA vendor 2 a weight of 300.
2. Sign in as vendor 1 and open the round.
3. Look at the data the app sent.
bugs.What should happen: Vendor 1 receives only its own weight (or none).
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3–4 Oct 2026: each variant failed the same way on two fresh test events. Cause: trade_template_serializer.rb:877-879 sends every vendor's weights. Also reproduced on Demo Account 2 (4 Oct 2026, two fresh test events).

bugs.Bug: One badly formed attachment makes the event or round unreadable for everyone
bugs.What goes wrong: When an attachment is saved in the wrong shape (for example as plain text instead of a file entry), Procol accepts and stores it. From then on every attempt to open that round crashes, for the buyer and for the vendors — the event is effectively broken.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Publish an event.
2. Save the round's terms-and-conditions attachments with a value that is plain text instead of a file entry.
3. Open the round again (as buyer or vendor).
bugs.What should happen: The bad attachment is refused when it is saved; the round keeps working.
bugs.What actually happens: The save is accepted, and every later opening of the round crashes.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3–4 Oct 2026: each variant failed the same way on two fresh test events. (event_group.rb:329-338; trade_controller.rb).

bugs.Bug: The check that an attached file belongs to the buyer's own company can be bypassed
bugs.What goes wrong: Procol checks that a file linked to an event comes from the company's own storage. That check can be passed with an encoded link or a link to another host, so a file that is not the company's own is accepted. We proved only that the check lets such links through; we did not read another company's file.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Attach a file to an event using a link whose address is encoded, or points to another storage host.
2. Save the event.
bugs.What should happen: The link is refused because the file is not in the company's own storage.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3–4 Oct 2026: each variant failed the same way on two fresh test events. (s3_url_validator.rb:25-33).

bugs.Bug: Changing only a round's terms-and-conditions files deletes its written clauses
bugs.What goes wrong: A round's terms and conditions have written clauses and attached files. Updating only the files deletes every written clause, without any warning.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Give a round written T&C clauses and a T&C file.
2. Update only the round's T&C files.
3. Read the round's T&C.
bugs.What should happen: The written clauses stay as they were.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3–4 Oct 2026: each variant failed the same way on two fresh test events. (trade_controller.rb:714-720).

bugs.Bug: An upload reports success for content it did not store
bugs.What goes wrong: When a file upload sends content Procol does not store, the upload still answers 'Successfully uploaded File', so the user believes the file is attached when it is not.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Upload a file to a round with content that Procol does not keep (for example an empty or unsupported upload).
2. Read the round's files.
bugs.What should happen: The upload is refused, or reports that nothing was stored.
bugs.What actually happens: 'Successfully uploaded File' — and nothing is attached.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3–4 Oct 2026: each variant failed the same way on two fresh test events. (s3_upload.rb:83-101).

bugs.Bug: Saving any partial change to a draft round crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: Updating a draft round with only some of its fields — even with nothing in the update — crashes the server, so a draft round cannot be edited one field at a time.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Create a draft event with a round.
2. Update the round with only one changed field (or with an empty update).
bugs.What should happen: The change is saved (or an empty update does nothing).
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3–4 Oct 2026: each variant failed the same way on two fresh test events. (trade_controller.rb:603 sends drafts to edit_draft).

bugs.Bug: Clarification questions crash for an unknown or draft event and on malformed filters
bugs.What goes wrong: Vendors and the buyer exchange clarification questions inside an event. Asking for or creating clarifications on an event that does not exist or is still a draft, or sending malformed filters, context or attachments, crashes the server instead of answering 'not found' or refusing the request.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Open clarifications for an event id that does not exist (or a draft event).
2. Or send a clarification with malformed filters or attachments.
bugs.What should happen: 'Not found', or a clear refusal.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on both clients (18 variants on PROCOL DEMO, 8 on Demo Account 2), each on two fresh test events (v1/chats_controller.rb).

bugs.Bug: Sending or listing reminders crashes on malformed or unknown input
bugs.What goes wrong: The buyer can send reminders to vendors who still have to act. Sending reminders without the list of recipients, with the recipients written as text, with an unknown reminder type, or for an event that does not exist crashes the server instead of refusing.
bugs.How to see it: 1. Send reminders for an event without saying who should get them (or with an unknown reminder type, or for an event that does not exist).
bugs.What should happen: A clear refusal or 'not found'.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3–4 Oct 2026: each variant failed the same way on two fresh test events. (reminders_controller.rb; reminders/base_service.rb:40).

bugs.Bug: Malformed attachments on a round or a surrogate bid crash, and the attachment link crashes without a token
bugs.What goes wrong: Sending a round's attachments in the wrong shape, or a bid entered on a vendor's behalf with a reference note but no files, crashes the server. The attachment-link address also crashes when it is called without a token instead of refusing.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Update a round with attachments in the wrong shape (or enter a surrogate bid with a note and no files).
2. Or open an attachment link without its token.
bugs.What should happen: A clear refusal.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on two fresh test events per variant; the attachment-link variant on both clients (trade_controller.rb:459; v1/attachments_controller.rb:12-18).

bugs.Bug: Saving malformed weights crashes
bugs.What goes wrong: Saving vendor weights in the wrong shape (for example text where a number belongs) crashes the server instead of refusing the weights.
bugs.How to see it: 1. On a round with weighted bidding, save the weights with a value in the wrong shape.
bugs.What should happen: A clear refusal naming the bad weight.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3–4 Oct 2026: each variant failed the same way on two fresh test events. (trade_controller.rb:1779,1804). Also reproduced on Demo Account 2 (6 variants, two fresh test events each).

bugs.Bug: Sending an empty value for any list of ids crashes the server
bugs.What goes wrong: Many requests carry lists of ids (for example the line items to reopen). Sending an empty value instead of a list for any such field crashes the server before the request is even looked at, because a shared check does not expect it.
bugs.How to see it: 1. Reopen line items on a round with the list of line items sent as an empty value.
bugs.What should happen: A clear refusal, or the request treated as an empty list.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on PROCOL DEMO on 3–4 Oct 2026: each variant failed the same way on two fresh test events. (params_auth.rb:70-73 — applies to every such field). Also reproduced on Demo Account 2 (two fresh test events).

bugs.Bug: Opening a vendor's bid details before that vendor has bid crashes the server
bugs.What goes wrong: The buyer can open the details of a vendor's bid on a round. If that vendor has not bid yet, the server crashes instead of answering that there is no bid, because it tries to read a bid that does not exist.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Publish a round and invite a QA vendor.
2. Before the vendor bids, open that vendor's bid details as the buyer.
bugs.What should happen: A clear 'Bid not found' answer.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on two fresh test events on PROCOL DEMO (bids_controller.rb:370-386).

bugs.Bug: A chat message that mentions the same colleague twice is refused as 'not allowed'
bugs.What goes wrong: In a round's chat a buyer can mention colleagues. Mentioning the same person twice in one message is refused with 'You are not allowed to perform this action', although mentioning them once, or sending a plain message, works. The check compares the list of mentioned people with a copy that has the duplicates removed.
bugs.How to see it: 1. On a live round, post a chat message that mentions the same colleague twice.
bugs.What should happen: The message is posted (the person is notified once).
bugs.What actually happens: Refused: 'You are not allowed to perform this action'.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on two fresh test events on PROCOL DEMO (expression_evaluator_service.rb:30-33).

bugs.Bug: After an amendment, the evaluation window starts and ends before bidding has even closed
bugs.What goes wrong: A technical round has a bidding window and then an evaluation window that starts when bidding ends. When the buyer issues an amendment (a new version of the event), Procol copies every window of the round but starts all of them at the moment of the amendment. The evaluation window therefore opens together with bidding and, being short, is already over long before bidding closes — so evaluators have no window left once the bids are in.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Publish an event with a technical round (bidding 10 minutes, then a short evaluation window).
2. Issue an amendment (a new version of the event).
3. Read the amended round's bidding and evaluation windows.
bugs.What should happen: Bidding runs from the amendment for its configured length, and evaluation starts when bidding ends — as on the original event.
bugs.What actually happens: Both windows start at the moment of the amendment: bidding 06:32:27 → 06:42:27, evaluation 06:32:27 → 06:32:32 (over ten minutes before bidding closes).
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on two fresh test events on PROCOL DEMO (4 Oct 2026), read from the amended round's stored windows; on each original event evaluation correctly started when bidding ended. Cause: versions/trade_request.rb replicate_trade_schedules sets every copied window to start now. Whether publishing the amendment re-times the windows was not checked.

bugs.Bug: A rescheduled start comes back a minute earlier than the buyer picked
bugs.What goes wrong: The event screen shows every time adjusted for the gap between the buyer's computer clock and Procol's server clock, but the Reschedule dialog saves the picked time without that adjustment. Whenever the two clocks differ, the saved start is off by that gap and the screen then shows a different time from the one the buyer chose. On UAT the browser was 1 second behind the server, so 2:30 pm came back as 2:29 pm.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Publish an event that starts later (upcoming).
2. Event Settings → Reschedule Event.
3. Pick a new start, e.g. 2:30 pm, and press Ok.
4. Open Reschedule Event again (or look at the event's start time).
bugs.What should happen: The event starts at the time the buyer picked and the screen shows that same time (2:30 pm).
bugs.What actually happens: The save sends 14:30:00 in the buyer's browser time; the screen then shows 2:29 pm, because it adds the clock gap (timeDiff = −1 s) when it shows the time. With a larger clock gap, the difference is larger.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on four fresh test events on PROCOL DEMO with QA vendors only (5 Oct 2026); the save call and the clock gap were recorded each time. Cause in client-dashboard: rescheduleEventModal.jsx sends scheduledDateTime.unix() unshifted, while selectors.js shows start = adjustForClient(starting_from) (server time + timeDiff).

bugs.Bug: A traffic-light range entered in the wrong order is refused with the message "Traffic light type is required"
bugs.What goes wrong: When a buyer sets up a traffic-light auction and enters the GREEN limit above the YELLOW limit, Save is correctly refused, but the only message says the traffic light TYPE is required. The type is already chosen and both limits are filled; the actual problem is their order. A buyer is told to fix the wrong thing.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Create a single-stage event, Event Type Auction, strategy Traffic Light, award the entire lot.
2. Enter GREEN "Gross total less than" 100 and YELLOW 50 (green above yellow).
3. Press Save.
bugs.What should happen: Save is refused with a message about the range (e.g. "Green must be lower than yellow").
bugs.What actually happens: Save is refused and the drawer shows "Traffic light type is required". The same message appears for a missing value, so the buyer cannot tell what is wrong.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced live on fresh create screens on PROCOL DEMO (6 Oct 2026) with two inverted pairs (100/50, 6000/3000); valid pairs (3000/6000, 50/100) save. Cause in client-dashboard: auctionConfiguration.jsx:681-707 sets one flag (errors.trafficLight) for "missing" and "lower above upper", and configuration.jsx:338-344 shows trafficLightValueRequired for it.

bugs.Bug: Publish is refused with "RFP duration exceeds RFQ end time" when the technical stage uses a fixed end time, even though it ends before the RFQ
bugs.What goes wrong: On a project with a technical (RFP) stage and an RFQ stage, the app checks that the technical stage ends no later than the RFQ. The check compares each stage's stored end value directly, but that value is a length in seconds when the end is set as a Duration and a clock timestamp when it is set as a Fixed time. With the technical stage on Fixed time and the RFQ on Duration, a timestamp is compared with a duration, so publish is always refused. In the other direction (technical on Duration, RFQ on Fixed time) the check can never fire, so a technical stage that really runs past the RFQ is let through.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Create an eRFX project with a Technical stage and an RFQ stage, a template, line items, an evaluator and one participant.
2. Open the schedule. Technical Stage: End time = Fixed time, 3 minutes from now. RFQ: End time = Duration, 30 Mins.
3. Save Schedule and Publish.
bugs.What should happen: Publish succeeds: the technical stage ends (e.g. 04:58 PM) before the RFQ (05:25 PM).
bugs.What actually happens: Publish is refused with "RFP duration exceeds RFQ end time. Please adjust." With both stages on Duration (30 Mins each) the same event publishes.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on two fresh events on PROCOL DEMO (8 Oct 2026, one run by the user, one by spine.ai with the panel captured before Save: technical ends 04:58 PM, RFQ ends 05:25 PM, refused). Cause in client-dashboard: projectCreation.jsx:1609-1622 compares stageConfig[].eventEndTime, which projectScheduler.jsx:99 sets to endTimeValue — a duration for EVENT_TIME_SCHEDULE_TYPE.relative and a timestamp for absolute (projectScheduler/helpers.js:24-27). Also on a new version (9 Oct 2026): the copied stages keep the end time the server stored, so re-scheduling only one stage to a Duration is refused the same way.

bugs.Bug: After removing line items from a new version of a two-stage event, the version cannot be published
bugs.What goes wrong: On a published project with a Technical stage and an RFQ, "Create New Version" opens the copy for editing. Removing a line item in Manage Line Items marks it deleted when the version is saved, but the screen still sends that item in each stage's sheet and technical forms. The server refuses both stage saves with "Event group line item does not belong to the specified event group" (code 890), so the version cannot be published.
bugs.How to see it:
1. Create an eRFX project with a Technical stage and an RFQ, 3 line items, 1 QA vendor; publish it.
2. On the project page, click Create New Version and confirm.
3. In Manage Line Items, delete one item and Save.
4. Set the schedule (both stages), fill the Addendum Remarks and Publish.
bugs.What should happen: The version publishes with the remaining items; the removed item is no longer in either stage.
bugs.What actually happens: Publish is refused with "Event group line item does not belong to the specified event group". The stage saves (PATCH …/trade/:id/template_input) still list the removed item (its line item is status deleted in event_group_line_items), and the server rejects them with code 890.
bugs.How it was verified: Reproduced on two fresh events on PROCOL DEMO (9 Oct 2026): 10 → 5 items and 3 → 2 items. A version with no item removed publishes normally. The rejecting check is validate_egli_ids_belong_to_event_group (trade_controller_helper.rb:3447-3457); the recorded requests show the removed item in data[] and forms[] after the event-group save deleted it.

cases.preconditions: Buyer logged in; RFQ template 'Standard RFQ' exists; product KNOB FX151-2925 in the catalogue; QA vendor onboarded; auto title enabled.
cases.steps:
1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Click 'Events' in the left-hand menu (calendar icon). The Events page opens with the tabs Live, History and Drafts, a search box and a blue 'Create Event' button at the top right.
3. Click the blue 'Create Event' button at the top right.
4. Choose 'Single Stage' (text: Source through RFP / RFQ / Auction). The create screen opens; 'Event Type' shows RFP selected by default.
5. Click 'RFQ' under Event Type.
6. Hover 'Select Templates' and click the RFQ template named in Test Data from the menu that opens (ignore any other menu that is still in the page). The product sheet with columns Product, Product Variant, Quantity Requested, Delivery location, Price appears.
7. Click into the first 'Product' cell of the sheet, type the product name from Test Data and click it in the list (the product code shows next to the name). 'Product Variant' fills itself.
8. Click the 'Quantity Requested' cell, type 10 and press Tab. Click the 'Delivery location' cell and pick the plant from Test Data.
9. Look at the Title box at the top: it has filled itself as '<product name> - <location>'. Leave it.
10. Click 'Terms & Conditions' in the footer. In the drawer click 'Add clause', type 'Delivery within 15 days of PO' and click Save. Make sure the 'Mandatory' switch is OFF. Close the drawer.
11. Scroll to 'Participants'. A yellow strip says 'Invite N more participant based on the products'. Click the 'Invite Vendor' button in that strip. All the vendors mapped to the product are added and the strip disappears.
12. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens.
13. Click 'Start later', pick tomorrow's date in the calendar and 11:00 in the time box. Under End time choose Duration '1 hour'. Click 'Save Schedule'.
14. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
15. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.
cases.expected: The page changes to the project page: the title you chose, an RFX number (e.g. RFX-3123) with a copy icon, the tabs Project Details / <stage> / Master QCS, a 'Upcoming (with the start time shown)' badge and a countdown. Under 'Published Stages' the stage code (RFQ-xxxx), Participants 0/N, Bidding Starts At and Bidding Ends At are shown. Terms & Conditions on Project Details: 1 clause. Participants: all vendors mapped to the product.

7. Click into the first 'Product' cell of the sheet, type the product name from Test Data and click it in the list (the product code shows next to the name). 'Product Variant' fills itself.
8. Click the 'Quantity Requested' cell, type 10 and press Tab. Click the 'Delivery location' cell and pick the plant from Test Data.
9. Click the Title box at the top, delete whatever is there and type the title from Test Data (QA_Platform …).

3. Click the blue 'Create Event' button at the top right.
4. Choose 'Single Stage' (text: Source through RFP / RFQ / Auction). The create screen opens; 'Event Type' shows RFP selected by default.
5. Click 'RFQ' under Event Type.

7. Click into the first 'Product' cell of the sheet, type the product name from Test Data and click it in the list (the product code shows next to the name). 'Product Variant' fills itself.
8. Click the 'Quantity Requested' cell, type 10 and press Tab. Click the 'Delivery location' cell and pick the plant from Test Data.
9. Click the Title box at the top, delete whatever is there and type the title from Test Data (QA_Platform …).

2. Click 'Events' in the left-hand menu (calendar icon). The Events page opens with the tabs Live, History and Drafts, a search box and a blue 'Create Event' button at the top right.
3. Click the blue 'Create Event' button at the top right.
4. Choose 'Single Stage'. On the create screen click 'Auction' under Event Type.
5. Hover 'Select Templates' and click the auction template named in Test Data. The product sheet appears.
6. In 'Auction Configurations' pick the strategy 'Rank based' (leave the other settings as they are).
7. Click into the first 'Product' cell of the sheet, type the product name from Test Data and click it in the list (the product code shows next to the name). 'Product Variant' fills itself.
8. Click the 'Quantity Requested' cell, type 10 and press Tab. Click the 'Delivery location' cell and pick the plant from Test Data.
9. Look at the Title box at the top: it has filled itself as '<product name> - <location>'. Leave it.
10. Click 'Terms & Conditions' in the footer. Click 'Add clause', type 'Delivery within 15 days of PO'. Click 'Attach' and upload GTC.pdf. Switch 'Mandatory' ON. Close the drawer.
11. Scroll to 'Participants'. Click into the box 'Search vendors you want to add' (not the Evaluator box), type the QA vendor's name from Test Data and click the vendor in the list under 'VENDORS'. The vendor appears as a participant chip.
12. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens.
13. Keep 'Start now'. Under End time keep 'Duration' and click the '30 min' preset. Read the line 'Event will end at …' and write it down. Click 'Save Schedule'.
14. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
15. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.

cases.preconditions: Buyer logged in; RFP questionnaire 'Technical Evaluation' + evaluator 'QA Evaluator' exists; product KNOB FX151-2925 in the catalogue; QA vendor onboarded; auto title enabled.
cases.steps:
1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Click 'Events' in the left-hand menu (calendar icon). The Events page opens with the tabs Live, History and Drafts, a search box and a blue 'Create Event' button at the top right.
3. Click the blue 'Create Event' button at the top right.
4. Choose 'Single Stage'. Keep 'RFP' selected under Event Type.
5. Hover 'Select Templates' and click the RFP questionnaire template named in Test Data. The questionnaire appears instead of a price sheet.
6. Scroll to 'Vendor Assessment', click the first dropdown there (the Evaluator picker) and choose the evaluator user named in Test Data.
7. Answer the questionnaire's required questions with the sample answers in Test Data (there is no product sheet on an RFP).
8. Look at the Title box at the top: it has filled itself as '<product name> - <location>'. Leave it.
9. Click 'Terms & Conditions' in the footer. In the drawer click 'Add clause', type 'Delivery within 15 days of PO' and click Save. Make sure the 'Mandatory' switch is OFF. Close the drawer.
10. Scroll to 'Participants'. Click into the box 'Search vendors you want to add' (not the Evaluator box), type the QA vendor's name from Test Data and click the vendor in the list under 'VENDORS'. The vendor appears as a participant chip.
11. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens.
12. Keep 'Start now'. Under End time keep 'Duration' and click the '30 min' preset. Read the line 'Event will end at …' and write it down. Click 'Save Schedule'.
13. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
14. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.
cases.expected: The page changes to the project page: the title you chose, an RFX number (e.g. RFX-3123) with a copy icon, the tabs Project Details / <stage> / Master QCS, a 'Live' badge and a countdown. Under 'Published Stages' the stage code (RFQ-xxxx), Participants 0/N, Bidding Starts At and Bidding Ends At are shown. Terms & Conditions on Project Details: 1 clause. Participants: the one QA vendor. The RFP shows the questionnaire and the evaluator, no price sheet.

1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Click 'Events' in the left-hand menu (calendar icon). The Events page opens with the tabs Live, History and Drafts, a search box and a blue 'Create Event' button at the top right.
3. Click the blue 'Create Event' button at the top right.
4. Choose 'Single Stage'. Keep 'RFP' selected under Event Type.
5. Hover 'Select Templates' and click the RFP questionnaire template named in Test Data. The questionnaire appears instead of a price sheet.
6. Scroll to 'Vendor Assessment', click the first dropdown there (the Evaluator picker) and choose the evaluator user named in Test Data.
7. Answer the questionnaire's required questions with the sample answers in Test Data (there is no product sheet on an RFP).
8. Look at the Title box at the top: it has filled itself as '<product name> - <location>'. Leave it.
9. Click 'Terms & Conditions' in the footer. Click 'Add clause', type 'Delivery within 15 days of PO'. Click 'Attach' and upload GTC.pdf. Switch 'Mandatory' ON. Close the drawer.
10. Scroll to 'Participants'. Click into the box 'Search vendors you want to add' (not the Evaluator box), type the QA vendor's name from Test Data and click the vendor in the list under 'VENDORS'. The vendor appears as a participant chip.
11. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens.
12. Click 'Start later', pick tomorrow's date in the calendar and 11:00 in the time box. Under End time choose Duration '1 hour'. Click 'Save Schedule'.
13. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
14. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.
cases.expected: The page changes to the project page: the title you chose, an RFX number (e.g. RFX-3123) with a copy icon, the tabs Project Details / <stage> / Master QCS, a 'Upcoming (with the start time shown)' badge and a countdown. Under 'Published Stages' the stage code (RFQ-xxxx), Participants 0/N, Bidding Starts At and Bidding Ends At are shown. Terms & Conditions on Project Details: 1 clause + 1 attachment, marked mandatory. Participants: the one QA vendor. The RFP shows the questionnaire and the evaluator, no price sheet.
