1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Click 'Events' in the left-hand menu (calendar icon). The Events page opens with the tabs Live, History and Drafts, a search box and a blue 'Create Event' button at the top right.
3. Click the blue 'Create Event' button at the top right.
4. Choose 'Single Stage'. Keep 'RFP' selected under Event Type.
5. Hover 'Select Templates' and click the RFP questionnaire template named in Test Data. The questionnaire appears instead of a price sheet.
6. Scroll to 'Vendor Assessment', click the first dropdown there (the Evaluator picker) and choose the evaluator user named in Test Data.
7. Answer the questionnaire's required questions with the sample answers in Test Data (there is no product sheet on an RFP).
8. Click the Title box at the top, delete whatever is there and type the title from Test Data (QA_Platform …).
9. Click 'Terms & Conditions' in the footer. Click 'Add clause', type 'Delivery within 15 days of PO'. Click 'Attach' and upload GTC.pdf. Switch 'Mandatory' ON. Close the drawer.
10. Scroll to 'Participants'. A yellow strip says 'Invite N more participant based on the products'. Click the 'Invite Vendor' button in that strip. All the vendors mapped to the product are added and the strip disappears.
11. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens.
12. Keep 'Start now'. Under End time choose 'Duration' → 'Custom' and type 2 hours. Under Evaluation time choose 30 minutes. Read 'Event will end at …'. Click 'Save Schedule'.
13. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
14. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.

7. Hover '+' again and click 'RFQ'. An 'RFQ' tab appears. Click ⋮ on the 'Technical' tab → Delete. Only the 'RFQ' tab remains. Click it so its panel shows.

1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Click 'Events' in the left-hand menu (calendar icon). The Events page opens with the tabs Live, History and Drafts, a search box and a blue 'Create Event' button at the top right.
3. Click the blue 'Create Event' button at the top right.
4. Choose 'eRFX Project' (text: Manage sourcing via a project approach). The project screen opens with a project Title box and a stage strip showing one stage tab 'Auction'.
5. Hover the round '+' icon next to the stage tab; a menu titled 'Add Stages' opens. Click 'Technical'. A second tab 'Technical' appears.
6. Click the three-dots (⋮) on the 'Auction' tab and click 'Delete'. The Auction tab disappears.
7. Hover '+' again and click 'RFQ'. An 'RFQ' tab appears. Click ⋮ on the 'Technical' tab → Delete. Only the 'RFQ' tab remains. Click it so its panel shows.
8. On the RFQ tab click 'Select Template' and pick the RFQ template named in Test Data.
9. Click the 'Items 0' button in the toolbar. The 'Manage Line Items' drawer opens on the right.
10. Click into the box 'Search and add line items', type the product name from Test Data and click it in the list that appears below. Enter the quantity 10 and choose the delivery location. Click 'Save'. The toolbar now shows 'Items 1'.
11. Click the Title box at the top, delete whatever is there and type the title from Test Data (QA_Platform …).
12. Click 'Terms & Conditions' in the footer. In the drawer click 'Add clause', type 'Delivery within 15 days of PO' and click Save. Make sure the 'Mandatory' switch is OFF. Close the drawer.
13. Scroll to 'Participants'. Click into the box 'Search vendors you want to add' (not the Evaluator box), type the QA vendor's name from Test Data and click the vendor in the list under 'VENDORS'. The vendor appears as a participant chip.
14. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens.
15. Click 'Start later', pick tomorrow's date in the calendar and 11:00 in the time box. Under End time choose Duration '1 hour'. Click 'Save Schedule'.
16. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
17. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.
cases.expected: The page changes to the project page: the title you chose, an RFX number (e.g. RFX-3123) with a copy icon, the tabs Project Details / <stage> / Master QCS, a 'Upcoming (with the start time shown)' badge and a countdown. Under 'Published Stages' the stage code (RFQ-xxxx), Participants 0/N, Bidding Starts At and Bidding Ends At are shown. Terms & Conditions on Project Details: 1 clause. Participants: the one QA vendor.

cases.title: Create and publish a single-stage RFQ from material PR, auto title, T&C none, vendors mapped, schedule now 30 min
cases.preconditions: Buyer logged in; RFQ template 'Standard RFQ' exists; an open material PR line; QA vendor onboarded; auto title enabled.
cases.steps:
1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Click 'Purchase Requisitions' in the left-hand menu. The PR list opens with the tabs Open, In Progress, Completed, Rejected, Deleted and a table of PR lines.
3. Stay on the Open tab. Find a line whose Item Type badge shows 'M' (material) and whose quantity is fully open (nothing in progress). Tick the checkbox at the start of that row.
4. Click the 'Purchase Items' button (cart icon, top right; its badge shows 1). A pop-up asks how you want to source the line.
5. Choose 'Single Stage' (text: Source through RFP / RFQ / Auction). The create screen opens; 'Event Type' shows RFP selected by default.
6. Click 'RFQ' under Event Type.
7. Hover 'Select Templates' and click the RFQ template named in Test Data from the menu that opens (ignore any other menu that is still in the page). The product sheet with columns Product, Product Variant, Quantity Requested, Delivery location, Price appears.
8. Check the product sheet: the PR line is already there with its product, variant, quantity with unit and delivery location copied from the PR. Do not change them.
9. Look at the Title box at the top: it has filled itself as '<product name> - <location>'. Leave it.
10. Do not open Terms & Conditions.
11. Scroll to 'Participants'. A yellow strip says 'Invite N more participant based on the products'. Click the 'Invite Vendor' button in that strip. All the vendors mapped to the product are added and the strip disappears.
12. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens.
13. Keep 'Start now'. Under End time keep 'Duration' and click the '30 min' preset. Read the line 'Event will end at …' and write it down. Click 'Save Schedule'.
14. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
15. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.
cases.expected: The page changes to the project page: the title you chose, an RFX number (e.g. RFX-3123) with a copy icon, the tabs Project Details / <stage> / Master QCS, a 'Live' badge and a countdown. Under 'Published Stages' the stage code (RFQ-xxxx), Participants 0/N, Bidding Starts At and Bidding Ends At are shown. Terms & Conditions on Project Details: none. Participants: all vendors mapped to the product. The PR line now shows under In Progress with this RFX number.

cases.preconditions: Buyer logged in; RFQ template 'Standard RFQ' exists; an open material PR line; QA vendor onboarded.
cases.steps:
1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Click 'Purchase Requisitions' in the left-hand menu. The PR list opens with the tabs Open, In Progress, Completed, Rejected, Deleted and a table of PR lines.
3. Stay on the Open tab. Find a line whose Item Type badge shows 'M' (material) and whose quantity is fully open (nothing in progress). Tick the checkbox at the start of that row.
4. Click the 'Purchase Items' button (cart icon, top right; its badge shows 1). A pop-up asks how you want to source the line.
5. Choose 'Single Stage' (text: Source through RFP / RFQ / Auction). The create screen opens; 'Event Type' shows RFP selected by default.
6. Click 'RFQ' under Event Type.
7. Hover 'Select Templates' and click the RFQ template named in Test Data from the menu that opens (ignore any other menu that is still in the page). The product sheet with columns Product, Product Variant, Quantity Requested, Delivery location, Price appears.
8. Check the product sheet: the PR line is already there with its product, variant, quantity with unit and delivery location copied from the PR. Do not change them.
9. Click the Title box at the top, delete whatever is there and type the title from Test Data (QA_Platform …).
10. Click 'Terms & Conditions' in the footer. Click 'Add clause', type 'Delivery within 15 days of PO'. Click 'Attach' and upload GTC.pdf. Switch 'Mandatory' ON. Close the drawer.
11. Scroll to 'Participants'. A yellow strip says 'Invite N more participant based on the products'. Click the 'Invite Vendor' button in that strip. All the vendors mapped to the product are added and the strip disappears.
12. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens.
13. Click 'Start later', pick tomorrow's date in the calendar and 11:00 in the time box. Under End time choose Duration '1 hour'. Click 'Save Schedule'.
14. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
15. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.
cases.expected: The page changes to the project page: the title you chose, an RFX number (e.g. RFX-3123) with a copy icon, the tabs Project Details / <stage> / Master QCS, a 'Upcoming (with the start time shown)' badge and a countdown. Under 'Published Stages' the stage code (RFQ-xxxx), Participants 0/N, Bidding Starts At and Bidding Ends At are shown. Terms & Conditions on Project Details: 1 clause + 1 attachment, marked mandatory. Participants: all vendors mapped to the product. The PR line now shows under In Progress with this RFX number.

2. Click 'Purchase Requisitions' in the left-hand menu. The PR list opens with the tabs Open, In Progress, Completed, Rejected, Deleted and a table of PR lines.
3. Stay on the Open tab. Find a line whose Item Type badge shows 'M' (material) and whose quantity is fully open (nothing in progress). Tick the checkbox at the start of that row.
4. Click the 'Purchase Items' button (cart icon, top right; its badge shows 1). A pop-up asks how you want to source the line.
5. Choose 'Single Stage'. On the create screen click 'Auction' under Event Type.
6. Hover 'Select Templates' and click the auction template named in Test Data. The product sheet appears.
7. In 'Auction Configurations' pick the strategy 'Rank based' (leave the other settings as they are).
8. Check the product sheet: the PR line is already there with its product, variant, quantity with unit and delivery location copied from the PR. Do not change them.
9. Look at the Title box at the top: it has filled itself as '<product name> - <location>'. Leave it.
10. Click 'Terms & Conditions' in the footer. In the drawer click 'Add clause', type 'Delivery within 15 days of PO' and click Save. Make sure the 'Mandatory' switch is OFF. Close the drawer.
11. Scroll to 'Participants'. Click into the box 'Search vendors you want to add' (not the Evaluator box), type the QA vendor's name from Test Data and click the vendor in the list under 'VENDORS'. The vendor appears as a participant chip.
12. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens.
13. Click 'Start later', pick tomorrow's date in the calendar and 11:00 in the time box. Under End time choose Duration '1 hour'. Click 'Save Schedule'.
14. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
15. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.

Participants: the one QA vendor. The PR line now shows under In Progress with this RFX number.

3. Stay on the Open tab. Find a line whose Item Type badge shows 'M' (material) and whose quantity is fully open (nothing in progress). Tick the checkbox at the start of that row.

13. Keep 'Start now'. Under End time choose 'Duration' → 'Custom' and type 2 hours. Under Evaluation time choose 30 minutes. Read 'Event will end at …'. Click 'Save Schedule'.

cases.preconditions: Buyer logged in; RFP questionnaire 'Technical Evaluation' + evaluator 'QA Evaluator' exists; an open material PR line; QA vendor onboarded; auto title enabled.
cases.steps:
1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Click 'Purchase Requisitions' in the left-hand menu. The PR list opens with the tabs Open, In Progress, Completed, Rejected, Deleted and a table of PR lines.
3. Stay on the Open tab. Find a line whose Item Type badge shows 'M' (material) and whose quantity is fully open (nothing in progress). Tick the checkbox at the start of that row.
4. Click the 'Purchase Items' button (cart icon, top right; its badge shows 1). A pop-up asks how you want to source the line.
5. Choose 'Single Stage'. Keep 'RFP' selected under Event Type.
6. Hover 'Select Templates' and click the RFP questionnaire template named in Test Data. The questionnaire appears instead of a price sheet.
7. Scroll to 'Vendor Assessment', click the first dropdown there (the Evaluator picker) and choose the evaluator user named in Test Data.
8. Check the product sheet: the PR line is already there with its product, variant, quantity with unit and delivery location copied from the PR. Do not change them.
9. Look at the Title box at the top: it has filled itself as '<product name> - <location>'. Leave it.
10. Click 'Terms & Conditions' in the footer. In the drawer click 'Add clause', type 'Delivery within 15 days of PO' and click Save. Make sure the 'Mandatory' switch is OFF. Close the drawer.
11. Scroll to 'Participants'. Click into the box 'Search vendors you want to add' (not the Evaluator box), type the QA vendor's name from Test Data and click the vendor in the list under 'VENDORS'. The vendor appears as a participant chip.
12. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens.
13. Keep 'Start now'. Under End time choose 'Duration' → 'Custom' and type 2 hours. Under Evaluation time choose 30 minutes. Read 'Event will end at …'. Click 'Save Schedule'.
14. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
15. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.
cases.expected: The page changes to the project page: the title you chose, an RFX number (e.g. RFX-3123) with a copy icon, the tabs Project Details / <stage> / Master QCS, a 'Live' badge and a countdown. Under 'Published Stages' the stage code (RFQ-xxxx), Participants 0/N, Bidding Starts At and Bidding Ends At are shown. Terms & Conditions on Project Details: 1 clause. Participants: the one QA vendor. The PR line now shows under In Progress with this RFX number. The RFP shows the questionnaire and the evaluator, no price sheet.

cases.preconditions: Buyer logged in; RFP questionnaire 'Technical Evaluation' + evaluator 'QA Evaluator' exists; an open material PR line; QA vendor onboarded; auto title enabled.
cases.steps:
1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Click 'Purchase Requisitions' in the left-hand menu. The PR list opens with the tabs Open, In Progress, Completed, Rejected, Deleted and a table of PR lines.
3. Stay on the Open tab. Find a line whose Item Type badge shows 'M' (material) and whose quantity is fully open (nothing in progress). Tick the checkbox at the start of that row.
4. Click the 'Purchase Items' button (cart icon, top right; its badge shows 1). A pop-up asks how you want to source the line.
5. Choose 'Single Stage'. Keep 'RFP' selected under Event Type.
6. Hover 'Select Templates' and click the RFP questionnaire template named in Test Data. The questionnaire appears instead of a price sheet.
7. Scroll to 'Vendor Assessment', click the first dropdown there (the Evaluator picker) and choose the evaluator user named in Test Data.
8. Check the product sheet: the PR line is already there with its product, variant, quantity with unit and delivery location copied from the PR. Do not change them.
9. Look at the Title box at the top: it has filled itself as '<product name> - <location>'. Leave it.
10. Click 'Terms & Conditions' in the footer. Click 'Add clause', type 'Delivery within 15 days of PO'. Click 'Attach' and upload GTC.pdf. Switch 'Mandatory' ON. Close the drawer.
11. Scroll to 'Participants'. Click into the box 'Search vendors you want to add' (not the Evaluator box), type the QA vendor's name from Test Data and click the vendor in the list under 'VENDORS'. The vendor appears as a participant chip.
12. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens.
13. Click 'Start later', pick tomorrow's date in the calendar and 11:00 in the time box. Under End time choose Duration '1 hour'. Click 'Save Schedule'.
14. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
15. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.
cases.expected: The page changes to the project page: the title you chose, an RFX number (e.g. RFX-3123) with a copy icon, the tabs Project Details / <stage> / Master QCS, a 'Upcoming (with the start time shown)' badge and a countdown. Under 'Published Stages' the stage code (RFQ-xxxx), Participants 0/N, Bidding Starts At and Bidding Ends At are shown. Terms & Conditions on Project Details: 1 clause + 1 attachment, marked mandatory. Participants: the one QA vendor. The PR line now shows under In Progress with this RFX number. The RFP shows the questionnaire and the evaluator, no price sheet.

3. Stay on the Open tab. Find a line whose Item Type badge shows 'M' (material) and whose quantity is fully open (nothing in progress). Tick the checkbox at the start of that row.
4. Click the 'Purchase Items' button (cart icon, top right; its badge shows 1). A pop-up asks how you want to source the line.
5. Choose 'eRFX Project' (text: Manage sourcing via a project approach). The project screen opens with a project Title box and a stage strip showing one stage tab 'Auction'.
6. Hover the round '+' icon next to the stage tab; a menu titled 'Add Stages' opens. Click 'Technical'. A second tab 'Technical' appears.
7. Click the three-dots (⋮) on the 'Auction' tab and click 'Delete'. The Auction tab disappears.
8. Hover '+' again and click 'RFQ'. An 'RFQ' tab appears. Click ⋮ on the 'Technical' tab → Delete. Only the 'RFQ' tab remains. Click it so its panel shows.
9. On the RFQ tab click 'Select Template' and pick the RFQ template named in Test Data.
10. Check the product sheet: the PR line is already there with its product, variant, quantity with unit and delivery location copied from the PR. Do not change them.
11. Look at the Title box at the top: it has filled itself as '<product name> - <location>'. Leave it.
12. Do not open Terms & Conditions.
13. Scroll to 'Participants'. A yellow strip says 'Invite N more participant based on the products'. Click the 'Invite Vendor' button in that strip. All the vendors mapped to the product are added and the strip disappears.
14. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens.
15. Keep 'Start now'. Under End time keep 'Duration' and click the '30 min' preset. Read the line 'Event will end at …' and write it down. Click 'Save Schedule'.
16. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
17. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.

cases.preconditions: Buyer logged in; questionnaire 'Technical Evaluation', assessment template 'Vendor Assessment', evaluator 'QA Evaluator', RFQ template 'Standard RFQ' exists; an open material PR line; QA vendor onboarded; auto title enabled.
cases.steps:
1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Click 'Purchase Requisitions' in the left-hand menu. The PR list opens with the tabs Open, In Progress, Completed, Rejected, Deleted and a table of PR lines.
3. Stay on the Open tab. Find a line whose Item Type badge shows 'M' (material) and whose quantity is fully open (nothing in progress). Tick the checkbox at the start of that row.
4. Click the 'Purchase Items' button (cart icon, top right; its badge shows 1). A pop-up asks how you want to source the line.
5. Choose 'eRFX Project'. The project screen opens with one stage tab 'Auction'.
6. Hover '+' → click 'Technical'. Click ⋮ on 'Auction' → Delete. Hover '+' → click 'RFQ'. You now have the tabs 'Technical' and 'RFQ'.
7. Click the 'Technical' tab → 'Select Template' → pick the questionnaire template in Test Data. In 'Vendor Assessment' click the template trigger inside that section and pick the assessment template; then pick the evaluator user.
8. Click the 'RFQ' tab → 'Select Template' → pick the RFQ template in Test Data.
9. Check the product sheet: the PR line is already there with its product, variant, quantity with unit and delivery location copied from the PR. Do not change them.
10. Look at the Title box at the top: it has filled itself as '<product name> - <location>'. Leave it.
11. Do not open Terms & Conditions.
12. Scroll to 'Participants'. A yellow strip says 'Invite N more participant based on the products'. Click the 'Invite Vendor' button in that strip. All the vendors mapped to the product are added and the strip disappears.
13. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens with one block per stage ('1. Technical Stage' and '2. RFQ' — scroll to see the second).
14. Keep 'Start now'. Under End time choose 'Duration' → 'Custom' and type 2 hours. Under Evaluation time choose 30 minutes. Read 'Event will end at …'. Click 'Save Schedule'.
15. Do the same in the second block (keep both blocks on Duration; the Technical block must end before the RFQ block).
16. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
17. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.
cases.expected: The page changes to the project page: the title you chose, an RFX number (e.g. RFX-3123) with a copy icon, the tabs Project Details / <stage> / Master QCS, a 'Live' badge and a countdown. Under 'Published Stages' the stage code (RFQ-xxxx), Participants 0/N, Bidding Starts At and Bidding Ends At are shown. Terms & Conditions on Project Details: none. Participants: all vendors mapped to the product. The PR line now shows under In Progress with this RFX number. Technical and RFQ both appear under Published Stages with the Technical end before the RFQ end.

cases.preconditions: Buyer logged in; questionnaire 'Technical Evaluation', assessment template 'Vendor Assessment', evaluator 'QA Evaluator', RFQ template 'Standard RFQ' exists; an open material PR line; QA vendor onboarded.
cases.steps:
1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Click 'Purchase Requisitions' in the left-hand menu. The PR list opens with the tabs Open, In Progress, Completed, Rejected, Deleted and a table of PR lines.
3. Stay on the Open tab. Find a line whose Item Type badge shows 'M' (material) and whose quantity is fully open (nothing in progress). Tick the checkbox at the start of that row.
4. Click the 'Purchase Items' button (cart icon, top right; its badge shows 1). A pop-up asks how you want to source the line.
5. Choose 'eRFX Project'. The project screen opens with one stage tab 'Auction'.
6. Hover '+' → click 'Technical'. Click ⋮ on 'Auction' → Delete. Hover '+' → click 'RFQ'. You now have the tabs 'Technical' and 'RFQ'.
7. Click the 'Technical' tab → 'Select Template' → pick the questionnaire template in Test Data. In 'Vendor Assessment' click the template trigger inside that section and pick the assessment template; then pick the evaluator user.
8. Click the 'RFQ' tab → 'Select Template' → pick the RFQ template in Test Data.
9. Check the product sheet: the PR line is already there with its product, variant, quantity with unit and delivery location copied from the PR. Do not change them.
10. Click the Title box at the top, delete whatever is there and type the title from Test Data (QA_Platform …).
11. Do not open Terms & Conditions.
12. Scroll to 'Participants'. A yellow strip says 'Invite N more participant based on the products'. Click the 'Invite Vendor' button in that strip. All the vendors mapped to the product are added and the strip disappears.
13. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens with one block per stage ('1. Technical Stage' and '2. RFQ' — scroll to see the second).
14. Keep 'Start now'. Under End time keep 'Duration' and click the '30 min' preset. Read the line 'Event will end at …' and write it down. Click 'Save Schedule'.
15. Do the same in the second block (keep both blocks on Duration; the Technical block must end before the RFQ block).
16. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
17. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.
cases.expected: The page changes to the project page: the title you chose, an RFX number (e.g. RFX-3123) with a copy icon, the tabs Project Details / <stage> / Master QCS, a 'Live' badge and a countdown. Under 'Published Stages' the stage code (RFQ-xxxx), Participants 0/N, Bidding Starts At and Bidding Ends At are shown. Terms & Conditions on Project Details: none. Participants: all vendors mapped to the product. The PR line now shows under In Progress with this RFX number. Technical and RFQ both appear under Published Stages with the Technical end before the RFQ end.

1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Click 'Purchase Requisitions' in the left-hand menu. The PR list opens with the tabs Open, In Progress, Completed, Rejected, Deleted and a table of PR lines.
3. Stay on the Open tab. Find a line whose Item Type badge shows 'M' (material) and whose quantity is fully open (nothing in progress). Tick the checkbox at the start of that row.
4. Click the 'Purchase Items' button (cart icon, top right; its badge shows 1). A pop-up asks how you want to source the line.
5. Choose 'eRFX Project'. The project screen opens with one stage tab 'Auction'.
6. Hover '+' → click 'Technical'. Click ⋮ on 'Auction' → Delete. Hover '+' → click 'RFQ'. You now have the tabs 'Technical' and 'RFQ'.
7. Click the 'Technical' tab → 'Select Template' → pick the questionnaire template in Test Data. In 'Vendor Assessment' click the template trigger inside that section and pick the assessment template; then pick the evaluator user.
8. Click the 'RFQ' tab → 'Select Template' → pick the RFQ template in Test Data.
9. Check the product sheet: the PR line is already there with its product, variant, quantity with unit and delivery location copied from the PR. Do not change them.
10. Click the Title box at the top, delete whatever is there and type the title from Test Data (QA_Platform …).
11. Click 'Terms & Conditions' in the footer. In the drawer click 'Add clause', type 'Delivery within 15 days of PO' and click Save. Make sure the 'Mandatory' switch is OFF. Close the drawer.
12. Scroll to 'Participants'. A yellow strip says 'Invite N more participant based on the products'. Click the 'Invite Vendor' button in that strip. All the vendors mapped to the product are added and the strip disappears.
13. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens with one block per stage ('1. Technical Stage' and '2. RFQ' — scroll to see the second).
14. Keep 'Start now'. Under End time keep 'Duration' and click the '30 min' preset. Read the line 'Event will end at …' and write it down. Click 'Save Schedule'.
15. Do the same in the second block (keep both blocks on Duration; the Technical block must end before the RFQ block).
16. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
17. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.
cases.expected: The page changes to the project page: the title you chose, an RFX number (e.g. RFX-3123) with a copy icon, the tabs Project Details / <stage> / Master QCS, a 'Live' badge and a countdown. Under 'Published Stages' the stage code (RFQ-xxxx), Participants 0/N, Bidding Starts At and Bidding Ends At are shown. Terms & Conditions on Project Details: 1 clause. Participants: all vendors mapped to the product. The PR line now shows under In Progress with this RFX number. Technical and RFQ both appear under Published Stages with the Technical end before the RFQ end.

1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Click 'Purchase Requisitions' in the left-hand menu. The PR list opens with the tabs Open, In Progress, Completed, Rejected, Deleted and a table of PR lines.
3. Stay on the Open tab. Find a line whose Item Type badge shows 'S' (service) — it shows '1 Service' instead of a material code. Tick its checkbox.
4. Click the 'Purchase Items' button (cart icon, top right). A pop-up asks how you want to source the line.
5. Choose 'Single Stage' (text: Source through RFP / RFQ / Auction). The create screen opens; 'Event Type' shows RFP selected by default.
6. Click 'RFQ' under Event Type.
7. Hover 'Select Templates' and click the RFQ template named in Test Data from the menu that opens (ignore any other menu that is still in the page). The product sheet with columns Product, Product Variant, Quantity Requested, Delivery location, Price appears.
8. Check the product sheet: the PR line is already there with its product, variant, quantity with unit and delivery location copied from the PR. Do not change them.
9. Click the Title box at the top, delete whatever is there and type the title from Test Data (QA_Platform …).
10. Do not open Terms & Conditions.
11. Scroll to 'Participants'. Click into the box 'Search vendors you want to add' (not the Evaluator box), type the QA vendor's name from Test Data and click the vendor in the list under 'VENDORS'. The vendor appears as a participant chip.
12. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens.
13. Keep 'Start now'. Under End time keep 'Duration' and click the '30 min' preset. Read the line 'Event will end at …' and write it down. Click 'Save Schedule'.
14. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
15. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.
cases.expected: The page changes to the project page: the title you chose, an RFX number (e.g. RFX-3123) with a copy icon, the tabs Project Details / <stage> / Master QCS, a 'Live' badge and a countdown. Under 'Published Stages' the stage code (RFQ-xxxx), Participants 0/N, Bidding Starts At and Bidding Ends At are shown. Terms & Conditions on Project Details: none. Participants: the one QA vendor. The PR line now shows under In Progress with this RFX number.

5. Choose 'eRFX Project' (text: Manage sourcing via a project approach). The project screen opens with a project Title box and a stage strip showing one stage tab 'Auction'.

7. Click the three-dots (⋮) on the 'Auction' tab and click 'Delete'. The Auction tab disappears.
8. Hover '+' again and click 'RFQ'. An 'RFQ' tab appears. Click ⋮ on the 'Technical' tab → Delete. Only the 'RFQ' tab remains. Click it so its panel shows.

10. Check the product sheet: the PR line is already there with its product, variant, quantity with unit and delivery location copied from the PR. Do not change them.

cases.preconditions: Buyer logged in; RFQ template 'Standard RFQ' exists; an open service PR line; QA vendor onboarded.
cases.steps:
1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Click 'Purchase Requisitions' in the left-hand menu. The PR list opens with the tabs Open, In Progress, Completed, Rejected, Deleted and a table of PR lines.
3. Stay on the Open tab. Find a line whose Item Type badge shows 'S' (service) — it shows '1 Service' instead of a material code. Tick its checkbox.
4. Click the 'Purchase Items' button (cart icon, top right). A pop-up asks how you want to source the line.
5. Choose 'eRFX Project' (text: Manage sourcing via a project approach). The project screen opens with a project Title box and a stage strip showing one stage tab 'Auction'.
6. Hover the round '+' icon next to the stage tab; a menu titled 'Add Stages' opens. Click 'Technical'. A second tab 'Technical' appears.
7. Click the three-dots (⋮) on the 'Auction' tab and click 'Delete'. The Auction tab disappears.
8. Hover '+' again and click 'RFQ'. An 'RFQ' tab appears. Click ⋮ on the 'Technical' tab → Delete. Only the 'RFQ' tab remains. Click it so its panel shows.
9. On the RFQ tab click 'Select Template' and pick the RFQ template named in Test Data.
10. Check the product sheet: the PR line is already there with its product, variant, quantity with unit and delivery location copied from the PR. Do not change them.
11. Click the Title box at the top, delete whatever is there and type the title from Test Data (QA_Platform …).
12. Click 'Terms & Conditions' in the footer. In the drawer click 'Add clause', type 'Delivery within 15 days of PO' and click Save. Make sure the 'Mandatory' switch is OFF. Close the drawer.
13. Scroll to 'Participants'. Click 'Invite Vendor' in the yellow strip to add the mapped vendors, then also search and add the QA vendor named in Test Data. Both appear as participants.
14. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens.
15. Keep 'Start now'. Under End time keep 'Duration' and click the '30 min' preset. Read the line 'Event will end at …' and write it down. Click 'Save Schedule'.
16. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.

2. Click 'Purchase Requisitions' in the left-hand menu. The PR list opens with the tabs Open, In Progress, Completed, Rejected, Deleted and a table of PR lines.
3. Stay on the Open tab. Find a line whose Item Type badge shows 'S' (service) — it shows '1 Service' instead of a material code. Tick its checkbox.
4. Click the 'Purchase Items' button (cart icon, top right). A pop-up asks how you want to source the line.
5. Choose 'eRFX Project'. The project screen opens with one stage tab 'Auction'.
6. Hover '+' → click 'Technical'. Click ⋮ on 'Auction' → Delete. Hover '+' → click 'RFQ'. You now have the tabs 'Technical' and 'RFQ'.
7. Click the 'Technical' tab → 'Select Template' → pick the questionnaire template in Test Data. In 'Vendor Assessment' click the template trigger inside that section and pick the assessment template; then pick the evaluator user.
8. Click the 'RFQ' tab → 'Select Template' → pick the RFQ template in Test Data.
9. Check the product sheet: the PR line is already there with its product, variant, quantity with unit and delivery location copied from the PR. Do not change them.
10. Click the Title box at the top, delete whatever is there and type the title from Test Data (QA_Platform …).
11. Click 'Terms & Conditions' in the footer. In the drawer click 'Add clause', type 'Delivery within 15 days of PO' and click Save. Make sure the 'Mandatory' switch is OFF. Close the drawer.
12. Scroll to 'Participants'. Click into the box 'Search vendors you want to add' (not the Evaluator box), type the QA vendor's name from Test Data and click the vendor in the list under 'VENDORS'. The vendor appears as a participant chip.
13. Click 'Schedule' in the footer. The 'Schedule Event' drawer opens with one block per stage ('1. Technical Stage' and '2. RFQ' — scroll to see the second).
14. Click 'Start later', pick tomorrow's date in the calendar and 11:00 in the time box. Under End time choose Duration '1 hour'. Click 'Save Schedule'.
15. Do the same in the second block (keep both blocks on Duration; the Technical block must end before the RFQ block).
16. Check the footer chip now shows the saved window.
17. Click the blue 'Publish Event' (or 'Publish') button in the footer. If a confirmation pop-up appears, click Confirm.
cases.expected: The page changes to the project page: the title you chose, an RFX number (e.g. RFX-3123) with a copy icon, the tabs Project Details / <stage> / Master QCS, a 'Upcoming (with the start time shown)' badge and a countdown. Under 'Published Stages' the stage code (RFQ-xxxx), Participants 0/N, Bidding Starts At and Bidding Ends At are shown. Terms & Conditions on Project Details: 1 clause. Participants: the one QA vendor. The PR line now shows under In Progress with this RFX number. Technical and RFQ both appear under Published Stages with the Technical end before the RFQ end.

cases.module: 4. Terms & Conditions — what the vendor must accept
cases.title: T&C switch OFF (all optional), no attachment; vendor accepts nothing
cases.preconditions: A live RFQ with 2 clauses set up as in the scenario; QA vendor invited.
cases.steps:
1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Create a single-stage RFQ (template, product, QA vendor, schedule Start now 30 min).
3. Click 'Terms & Conditions' in the footer; add the two clauses; set the mode: switch OFF (all optional). Close and Publish.
4. Open the Procol vendor portal in a separate browser (or incognito window) and log in as the QA test vendor (email qa_<stamp>@example.com, OTP). You land on the vendor's event list.
5. Open the event from the Live list. Scroll to the Terms & Conditions block: read the clauses and the Accept checkboxes.
6. Enter price 100 in the price sheet.
7. T&C: accepts nothing (tick the matching checkboxes).
8. Click 'Submit' and confirm.
cases.expected: The bid is submitted ('Bid submitted', revision 1). On the buyer's Responses tab the bid shows which clauses were accepted; unaccepted optional clauses are shown as not accepted but do not block anything.

1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Open a closed (or withdrawn) event, click its stage tab, click the 'Settings' gear at the top right and click 'Recreate Order'. The 'Recreate Order' pop-up opens.
3. Check the Product Sheet at the top: the product, variant, quantity and delivery location are pre-filled from the old event (scroll right to see Price).
4. Under 'Event End Time Duration' click '15 Mins'.
5. Under 'Evaluation Duration' click '15 Mins'.
6. Click the Delivery Date box and pick a date next month.
7. Tick 'Schedule this event?', pick tomorrow in 'Select date' and 11:00 in 'Select time'.
8. Click the blue 'Create Order' button at the bottom right.
cases.expected: A new event is created and opens: a new RFX / stage code, the same product and quantity, status Upcoming with start tomorrow 11:00, bidding end = start + 15 minutes (read it under Published Stages), evaluation 15 Mins after the end, delivery date shown on the line as chosen. The original event is unchanged. Note whether the old participants were copied (record).

1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Open a closed (or withdrawn) event, click its stage tab, click the 'Settings' gear at the top right and click 'Recreate Order'. The 'Recreate Order' pop-up opens.
3. Check the Product Sheet at the top: the product, variant, quantity and delivery location are pre-filled from the old event (scroll right to see Price).
4. Under 'Event End Time Duration' click '30 Mins'.
5. Under 'Evaluation Duration' click '30 Mins'.
6. Click the Delivery Date box and pick a date next month.
7. Tick 'Schedule this event?', pick tomorrow in 'Select date' and 11:00 in 'Select time'.
8. Click the blue 'Create Order' button at the bottom right.
cases.expected: A new event is created and opens: a new RFX / stage code, the same product and quantity, status Upcoming with start tomorrow 11:00, bidding end = start + 30 minutes (read it under Published Stages), evaluation 30 Mins after the end, delivery date shown on the line as chosen. The original event is unchanged. Note whether the old participants were copied (record).

1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Open a closed (or withdrawn) event, click its stage tab, click the 'Settings' gear at the top right and click 'Recreate Order'. The 'Recreate Order' pop-up opens.
3. Check the Product Sheet at the top: the product, variant, quantity and delivery location are pre-filled from the old event (scroll right to see Price).
4. Under 'Event End Time Duration' click 'Custom 90 minutes' and type 90 in the box that appears.
5. Under 'Evaluation Duration' click '45 Mins'.
6. Leave Delivery Date empty.
7. Leave 'Schedule this event?' unticked.
8. Click the blue 'Create Order' button at the bottom right.
cases.expected: A new event is created and opens: a new RFX / stage code, the same product and quantity, status Live, started now, bidding end = start + 90 minutes (read it under Published Stages), evaluation 45 Mins after the end, delivery date blank. The original event is unchanged. Note whether the old participants were copied (record).

cases.module: 6. Settings (gear) — Recreate Order, Extend, Reschedule, Rejected Bids, Order Activity, Evaluation time
cases.title: Reject a bid while bidding is live with re-bidding allowed, then vendor tries to bid again
cases.preconditions: An RFQ while bidding is live with a submitted bid from the QA vendor.
cases.steps:
1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Open the event (while bidding is live) → stage tab → Responses.
3. On the vendor's bid row click 'Reject'. A pop-up asks for a reason and whether to allow re-bidding.
4. First click Reject with the reason empty.
5. Type the reason, choose 're-bidding allowed', click Reject.
6. Open Settings → 'Rejected Bids' and read the list.
7. Open the Procol vendor portal in a separate browser (or incognito window) and log in as the QA test vendor (email qa_<stamp>@example.com, OTP). You land on the vendor's event list.
8. Open the event; read the status; click Edit/Submit bid and try to send a new price.
cases.expected: Empty reason: 'Please add a reason for rejecting this bid'. With a reason: the bid shows Rejected with the reason in Responses and in Settings → Rejected Bids (vendor, time, reason, re-bid flag); the vendor sees 'Rejected' with the reason. Vendor bidding again: accepted as a new bid while live; refused after close.

1. Open the Procol buyer website in Chrome and log in as the buyer user of the test company (enter the email or mobile, click Continue, enter the OTP you receive, click Verify). You land on the home dashboard.
2. Open the event (after bidding closed) → stage tab → Responses.
3. On the vendor's bid row click 'Reject'. A pop-up asks for a reason and whether to allow re-bidding.
4. First click Reject with the reason empty.

6. Open Settings → 'Rejected Bids' and read the list.
7. Back in Rejected Bids click 'Restore' (set active) on the bid.

With a reason: the bid shows Rejected with the reason in Responses and in Settings → Rejected Bids (vendor, time, reason, re-bid flag); the vendor sees 'Rejected' with the reason. Restore: refused after close (record the message).

cases.module: 8. Matching workflows and submitting the PO form
cases.title: Submit Proposal opens the approval modal listing ONLY the matching workflows
cases.preconditions: A PR-based RFQ on DLF Hospitality made from the template "DLF Capex NFA Test RFQ" (its PO template is "DLF PO - General Details (Test)", routing on), with a vendor response, awarded to the vendor so that the PO form is open as a draft. On UAT: RFX-2112 (PR-369 item 15, unit National Clubs -Kochi) with vendor Demo10. The test user created the draft. The test user's own QA_Platform workflows exist as named in each case (approver = the test user). Proposal value ₹9,000 (90 × ₹100).
cases.steps:
1. Log in to Procol (buyer side, cpanel.ag-ri.in) with the DLF Hospitality test user
2. From the left menu click "Events", open the awarded event (RFX-2112) and click "Create PO" / open its draft proposal. The page "PO Form / RFX-2112" opens with the "General Details" section on top and "Submit Proposal" at the top right
3. Fill General Details: Legal Entity DLF LIMITED, Department IT, Nature of Expense Budgeted with 3 quotes (Form Type and Unit Name are pre-filled)
4. Create two workflows: "QA_Platform AW SUB-A" (Unit Kochi AND Department IT) and "QA_Platform AW SUB-B" (Department IT or HR), both for team All Categories / Member, approver yourself
5. Click "Submit Proposal" at the top right
cases.expected: The modal lists SUB-A and SUB-B (and any other Member workflow that matches). Not listed: "GD Test - CAPEX…" (initiators Admin), the company "test" catch-alls (team workflows win), workflows for other units/departments. The page called GET /proposal/<id>/approval_workflows.

cases.module: 0. Set-up: Original Event & PO
cases.title: Create, publish, bid, award and generate PO for a goods event made without a PR
cases.preconditions: Vendors A and Vendor C are onboarded. PO Amendment through sourcing is ON for the company.
cases.steps:
1. Log in to Procol (buyer side) with the buyer user
2. Create an RFQ event directly (not from a PR) with the items, T&C, attachments and technical stage given in Test Data
3. Invite Vendors A and Vendor C and publish
4. Vendor A accepts T&C and bids in USD; Vendor C accepts T&C and bids in INR
5. Award all items to Vendor A and get the award approved
6. Generate the PO and note the PO number and event number
cases.expected: PO is generated and active for Vendor A. Later test cases call this "the goods PO (Bolt, Nut, Washer)".

cases.module: 0. Set-up: Original Event & PO

cases.expected: PO is generated for Vendor A. PR shows 3 lines in progress / ordered and 2 lines still open. Later test cases call this "the PR-based goods PO".

cases.module: 0. Set-up: choosing and reading the PR
cases.title: Open the PR that was named and read its header
cases.preconditions: The workspace has Purchase Requisitions. A PR number is given (e.g. 0110000195).
cases.steps:
1. Log in to Procol (buyer side) with the buyer user of the test workspace
2. Open Purchase Requisitions from the left menu
3. Type the PR number in the top-right Search (Shift+F) and open the row, or click the PR NO link in the list
4. Read the PR header: PR number, requester, plant/location, creation date, status tab (Open / In Progress / Completed / Rejected / Deleted)
cases.expected: The named PR opens; its number matches exactly; its lines are listed with Item Type, Item, PR Age, Material/Service code and quantities. If the number does not exist the search shows no rows and nothing else is opened.

cases.module: 0. Set-up: choosing and reading the PR
cases.title: Pick a random OPEN PR when none is named
cases.preconditions: At least one PR on the Open tab with a fully open line (Qty open = Qty requested).
cases.steps:
1. Log in to Procol (buyer side) with the buyer user of the test workspace
2. Open Purchase Requisitions → Open tab
3. Pick any row whose line is fully open and not on hold / dormant-locked
4. Note its PR number and item type for the next steps
cases.expected: A PR is chosen only from Open; its number and chosen line are recorded so every later step (event, award, PO) can be traced back to it. PRs under In Progress / Completed / Rejected / Deleted are never picked.

cases.module: 0. Set-up: choosing and reading the PR
cases.title: Tell a material PR from a service PR from the Item Type column
cases.preconditions: PRs of both kinds exist (screenshot: 0170000508 'S' Fencing Work, 0110000195 'M' GI coated sheet).
cases.steps:
1. Log in to Procol (buyer side) with the buyer user of the test workspace
2. Open Purchase Requisitions → Open
3. Look at the Item Type badge of each line: 'M' = material, 'S' = service
4. Open a service line: it shows '1 Service' with activities underneath; open a material line: it shows the Material code column filled and no Service Code
cases.expected: Material lines carry a Material code and a quantity with UOM; service lines carry a Service Code / activities (rate-based) and the badge S. The type decides the event: a material PR makes a goods event (product sheet with quantity), a service PR makes a service event (service + activities).

cases.module: 0. Set-up: choosing and reading the PR
cases.title: Recognise an asset (capex) line from the PR details

cases.steps:

2. Open the PR → click the line → 'Details'
3. Read Account Assignment, Asset number, Cost centre / WBS
cases.expected: The line is identified as an asset purchase (Account Assignment 'A' / asset number present). It is sourced like a material line but the award/PO must keep the asset account assignment. If the workspace has no asset lines, mark Not applicable.
